Strata Storage provides one key/value API for browser and Capacitor storage adapters, with explicit setup for native paths and optional features.
A single-page, machine-friendly map of strata-storage — entry points, every adapter and feature, framework bindings, and copy-paste integration recipes for AI coding agents.
Complete API documentation for Strata Storage.
Strata Storage presents the same key/value operations to different storage backends. The selected adapter determines where values live and which platform can read them.
Native file-system storage for iOS and Android via Capacitor.
Store small app settings in native iOS and Android preferences through Capacitor.
Store sensitive values through Strata Storage's native secure adapter in a Capacitor app.

The optional Capacitor SQLite adapter stores Strata key/value records in a native SQLite database on iOS and Android. Strata's public API remains key/value based: it does not expose raw SQL, indexes or atomic SQL transactions through storage.
Store Strata key-value data in the browser Cache API.
Store small, non-sensitive values in browser cookies.
Store structured key-value data in the browser's IndexedDB database.
Persistent browser storage using the localStorage API.
The memory adapter keeps values in a JavaScript Map. Its values disappear when the page or process is reloaded. Use it for data you can regenerate, short-lived previews and tests.
Session-scoped browser storage using the sessionStorage API.
Persists state in the page URL — shareable, bookmarkable, reload-surviving UI state.

This directory contains practical examples demonstrating how to use Strata Storage in various scenarios.

Strata's encryption manager runs only when the instance has encryption.enabled true on an instance without that configuration does not turn encryption on. These examples use the async API and a password supplied by the calling application.
Keep a bounded local analytics outbox with Strata Storage and send it to your own validated endpoint.
Wrap the supported Strata Storage API in an Angular service for local drafts and subscriptions.
Simple examples to get started with Strata Storage.
Learn how to perform Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations with Strata Storage.

A cache is useful only when a miss can be recovered. These examples cache JSON data in a browser adapter and let TTL remove stale entries. Strata's Cache adapter stores JSON-serializable key/value data; it is not the browser's Request/Response cache.

A Capacitor app can use the same set() and get() calls on web, iOS and Android after it registers the native adapters. A browser build exercises the web adapters; native persistence needs device testing.
Strata's bundled LZ codec runs when the instance has compression.enabled true option on an unconfigured instance does not initialize the compressor.
Use defineStorage() for a web-ready instance. It registers the standard web adapters and initializes on the first operation.

Strata can notify another browser tab about a change to a supported shared adapter. A notification helps a view refresh; it does not make two concurrent writes atomic or synchronize an authenticated session.
Queue browser writes with Strata Storage and replay them to an idempotent server endpoint.

Strata uses Web Crypto for encrypted values. Create an instance with encryption enabled, then provide a password at the operation or instance level. A plain defineStorage() instance does not initialize the encryption manager, even if a later set() passes encrypt: true.
Handle failed Strata Storage writes and reads using the public error classes and explicit fallback behavior.

A Strata instance can select from its registered adapters. The default list chooses the first available adapter at initialization; a later write error is not automatically retried elsewhere.

Strata can keep a local draft while the network is unavailable. Sending that draft to a server is an application protocol: the server must accept an idempotency key and return a successful HTTP status before the client removes its queued write.
Measure Strata Storage reads, writes and local query costs without invented benchmarks or unsupported indexes.

Strata Storage 3.1.4 does not register React Native storage adapters. The native adapters exported from strata-storage/capacitor use Capacitor plugins and require a Capacitor runtime. A React Native app cannot use them by selecting secure, sqlite or preferences in defaultStorages.
Keep a small browser cart with Strata Storage while leaving prices and checkout to the server.
Use Strata Storage TTL, absolute expiry and expiry inspection without treating client expiry as server authentication.

Strata Storage holds client-side key-value data. It does not authenticate a user, issue a session, or enforce server authorization. The host application must do those jobs. For a browser app, keep the session credential in a server-issued HttpOnly cookie; JavaScript and Strata's cookie adapter cannot create one.
Keep a small Vue value in browser storage and clean up the Strata Storage subscription on unmount.

Strata Storage gives browser and Capacitor apps one set() and get() shape across several storage adapters. The adapter still matters: browser, iOS and Android values live in different places, and a browser read cannot prove a native read.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First pass' }, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft', { storage: 'indexedDB', }); defineStorage() registers the standard browser adapters and initializes on first use. Memory, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies and a JSON-value Cache adapter are included. The URL adapter is registered separately for shareable UI state.

Runtime Available path Verification boundary Browser page Standard web adapters through defineStorage() Test the selected browser, quota and reload behaviour Capacitor iOS/Android Register Preferences, Secure, SQLite or Filesystem adapters Run write → read → restart → read on a device Node or server process Memory and explicitly supported adapters Do not assume a browser or native backend exists The native Secure adapter uses iOS Keychain or Android EncryptedSharedPreferences. Strata does not expose a biometric requirement or guarantee hardware-backed keys through its public options. Native adapter read paths still require device verification.

Encryption and compression need an instance configured for those transforms. An encrypted write also needs an encryption password. Follow the encryption and compression guides before enabling them. TTL can expire stored values. Query conditions match fields of the decoded value; wrapper metadata is not queryable. See TTL and the query reference. Cross-tab notifications can help refresh browser views. They do not make multi-tab writes atomic. Optional Firebase integration requires its own project and setup; it is not automatic cross-device sync.
Install the package. Run the Quick Start. Choose an adapter. Read the API reference.

This page is a dense, single-screen map of strata-storage for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, etc.). It exists so you can integrate the package into any project by matching the host project's needs to the right adapters and features — without reading the whole site. Package: strata-storage · current version 2.8.2 · MIT · zero runtime dependencies. Install: npm i strata-storage (or yarn add strata-storage). Node ≥ 24.13. Machine-readable companions: /llms.txt (index) and /llms-full.txt (the entire docs concatenated into one file for one-shot ingestion). A bundled AI-INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md also ships inside the npm package.

One unified async + sync key-value API over many backends — web (localStorage, IndexedDB, cookies, Cache API, memory, URL), native mobile via Capacitor (Preferences, Keychain/Keystore, SQLite, Filesystem), and optional remote (Firebase). Zero runtime dependencies; framework/native/Firebase deps are optional peer deps. Features (encryption, compression, TTL, queries, sync, integrity/recovery) are opt-in and compose across any backend.

Import Provides strata-storage Strata, defineStorage, the default storage, all web adapters, URLAdapter, feature helpers. strata-storage/capacitor PreferencesAdapter, SecureAdapter, SqliteAdapter, FilesystemAdapter. strata-storage/firebase enableFirebaseSync, isFirebaseAvailable. strata-storage/react createStrataHooks (provider-free) + <StrataProvider>. strata-storage/vue createStrataComposables + StrataPlugin. strata-storage/angular provideStrata / StrataService (RxJS).

storage Platform Sync API? Observable Queryable Use when memory all ✅ ✅ ✅ tests, ephemeral cache localStorage web ✅ ✅ ✅ small persistent data sessionStorage web ✅ ✅ ✅ per-session data indexedDB web ❌ ❌ ✅ large / structured data cookies web ✅ ❌ ✅ small server-readable data cache web ❌ ❌ ✅ offline assets / big blobs url web ✅ ✅ ✅ shareable UI state in the URL preferences Capacitor ❌ ❌ ✅ simple native settings secure Capacitor ❌ ❌ ✅ secrets (Keychain/Keystore) sqlite Capacitor ❌ ❌ ✅ structured / multi-store (database+table) filesystem Capacitor ❌ ❌ ✅ document-shaped values firestore Firebase ❌ ✅ ✅ cross-device/user document sync realtime Firebase ❌ ✅ ❌ low-latency shared state Sync-API adapters support getSync/setSync/...; the rest are async-only. Tools for migrating data between schema versions. Experimental: MigrationManager is exported from strata-storage, but it is a standalone, adapter-level utility — it is not configured through StrataConfig (there is no migrations option on new Strata(...)). It operates directly on an initialized storage adapter. import { MigrationManager, LocalStorageAdapter } from 'strata-storage'; const adapter = new LocalStorageAdapter(); await adapter.initialize(); const migrator = new MigrationManager(); migrator.register({ version: 1, up: async (a) => { /* transform stored data via a.get/a.set/... */ }, }); await migrator.migrate(adapter, 1);

// Register standard web adapters; operations initialize lazily. const storage = defineStorage(); // Set data await storage.set(key, value, options?); // Get data const value = await storage.get(key, options?); // Remove data await storage.remove(key, options?); // Check existence const exists = await storage.has(key, options?); // Clear storage await storage.clear(options?); // Get all keys const keys = await storage.keys(pattern?, options?); // Get size info const size = await storage.size(detailed?);

// Query data const results = await storage.query(condition, options?); // Subscribe to changes const unsubscribe = storage.subscribe(callback, options?); // Export data const exported = await storage.export(options?); // Import data await storage.import(data, options?); // Get TTL const ttl = await storage.getTTL(key, options?); // Extend TTL await storage.extendTTL(key, extension, options?); // Make persistent await storage.persist(key, options?);

// Generate secure password const password = storage.generatePassword(length?); // Hash data const hash = await storage.hash(data); // Get available storage types const types = storage.getAvailableStorageTypes(); // Get adapter capabilities const capabilities = storage.getCapabilities(storage?);

Strata Storage presents the same key/value operations to different storage backends. The selected adapter determines where values live and which platform can read them.

Adapter Where it runs What it stores Setup Memory JavaScript runtime Temporary values, cleared on reload Included in the default web set LocalStorage Browser page Persistent values for one origin Included in the default web set SessionStorage Browser page Values for one tab session Included in the default web set IndexedDB Browser page Persistent key/value data Included in the default web set Cookies Browser page Small values in browser cookies Included in the default web set Cache Browser page JSON-serializable key/value data backed by the Cache API Included in the default web set URL Browser page Small, shareable UI state in a query or hash Register URLAdapter explicitly Preferences Capacitor iOS/Android Native app preferences Register Capacitor adapters Secure Capacitor iOS/Android Values through Keychain or EncryptedSharedPreferences Register Capacitor adapters SQLite Capacitor iOS/Android Native SQLite-backed key/value data Register Capacitor adapters Filesystem Capacitor iOS/Android One JSON file per key Register Capacitor adapters Browser quota, native storage limits and latency vary by browser, device, data size and operation. The table does not promise a capacity or benchmark. Test the read path on every platform you ship; device verification remains required for native adapters.

defineStorage() registers the standard browser set and initializes on first operation. Without an explicit storage option, Strata tries the configured defaultStorages in order and uses the first available registered adapter. It does not rank adapters by speed, reliability or capacity. import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], }); await storage.set('draft', { title: 'Working copy' }); const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft'); To target a specific adapter, supply its name. A fallback list is tried in your chosen order: await storage.set('draft', { title: 'Working copy' }, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); await storage.set('session-note', 'editing', { storage: ['sessionStorage', 'memory'], }); Register native adapters before selecting preferences, secure, sqlite or filesystem: import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor'; const nativeStorage = defineStorage(); await registerCapacitorAdapters(nativeStorage); await nativeStorage.set('device-setting', 'on', { storage: 'preferences' }); The native example needs a Capacitor runtime and device verification. The Secure adapter uses platform facilities, but Strata's public options do not request biometric authentication or promise hardware-backed keys. Do not treat a browser test as proof of native behaviour.

The Strata API exposes key/value operations. Its IndexedDB and SQLite adapters use their underlying storage systems, but Strata does not expose native database transactions, indexes or raw SQL through storage. Use a platform API directly when you need those features. The Cache adapter stores serializable values, not Request/Response objects or service worker request caches; use the browser Cache API directly for those tasks. storage.getCapabilities(name) reports an adapter's declared capabilities after it is registered. Capability flags describe the adapter interface; they do not replace a runtime availability check or a read/write/read test. For custom adapter implementation and registration, follow the custom adapters guide. For optional Firebase adapters, follow the Firebase guide and select them explicitly after setup.

Native file-system storage for iOS and Android via Capacitor. v2.6.0: FilesystemAdapter now has a real native backend on iOS and Android. isAvailable() returns true on both platforms. Prior versions had no native implementation and the adapter was effectively unavailable on device. Pending on-device verification: The native code is complete and code-reviewed. Simulator and real-device sign-off is tracked in docs/guides/platforms/device-verification.md.

Each key is stored as a single JSON file inside a dedicated subdirectory of the app's sandboxed storage area: iOS: <NSDocumentsDirectory>/strata_storage/<sanitised-key>.json Android: <Context.getFilesDir()>/strata_storage/<sanitised-key>.json The file content is the full StorageValue wrapper serialised to JSON, so TTL, tags, and metadata are preserved across a write-read cycle. Writes go through an atomic staging step — the value is written to a temp file in a reserved strata_storage/.strata-staging/ subdirectory, then renamed into place. This is designed to avoid replacing a stored value with a partial write; the crash path still needs the device verification linked above. On the web (non-Capacitor) platform isAvailable() returns false and all calls are routed to the in-memory fallback.

Feature Support Persistence ✅ Yes (app-sandboxed filesystem) Synchronous ❌ No (async I/O) Observable ✅ Yes Searchable ✅ Limited (key-prefix scan) Iterable (keys()) ✅ Yes Capacity Limited by available app storage on the device Performance File I/O speed (variable; slower than SQLite for many small keys) TTL Support ✅ Yes (stored in value wrapper) Batch Support ✅ Yes Transaction Support ❌ No size(true) ✅ Yes (v2.6.0+)

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { FilesystemAdapter } from 'strata-storage/capacitor'; const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['filesystem'], }); storage.registerAdapter(new FilesystemAdapter()); await storage.refreshAdapters(); // Write a value await storage.set('report_q1', { lines: 42, status: 'final' }, { storage: 'filesystem', }); // Read it back const report = await storage.get<{ lines: number; status: string }>('report_q1', { storage: 'filesystem', }); console.log(report?.lines); // 42
All methods follow the standard BaseAdapter contract. Key behaviours specific to this adapter are noted below.

Returns true when running inside a Capacitor app on iOS or Android. Returns false in a browser context. const fsAdapter = new FilesystemAdapter(); const available = await fsAdapter.isAvailable(); // true on device, false in browser

Reads strata_storage/<sanitised-key>.json and deserialises the stored StorageValue<T> wrapper. Returns null when the file does not exist. Returns null (treating the entry as a miss) when the file content is not valid JSON — corrupt legacy files do not throw.

Serialises value to JSON and writes it via an atomic rename: Write to strata_storage/.strata-staging/<sanitised-key>.tmp Rename into strata_storage/<sanitised-key>.json This prevents partial files from appearing if the process is interrupted.
Deletes strata_storage/<sanitised-key>.json. No-op if the file does not exist.
Deletes every .json file in strata_storage/. Files in the staging subdirectory are also removed. Does not delete the directory itself.

Lists strata_storage/, reverses the file-name sanitisation for each .json file, and returns the original key strings. Temp files in .strata-staging/ are never included in this list — a key whose name resembles a temp file (e.g. "backup.tmp") is safely stored and returned by keys(). If pattern is provided the returned array is filtered by prefix or glob.

Sums the byte sizes of all .json files in strata_storage/. // Basic size const basic = await fsAdapter.size(); // { total: 4096, count: 12 } // Detailed breakdown (v2.6.0+) const detail = await fsAdapter.size(true); // { // total: 4096, // count: 12, // detailed: { keys: 240, values: 3600, metadata: 256 } // } detailed.keys is the byte sum of all key strings, detailed.values is the byte sum of serialised values, and detailed.metadata covers timestamps, tags, and metadata fields.

FilesystemAdapter currently takes no constructor options. The storage subdirectory name (strata_storage) and the staging directory (strata_storage/.strata-staging) are fixed. // No options — just instantiate const fsAdapter = new FilesystemAdapter();

Files are placed in the app's NSDocumentsDirectory, which means they are included in iCloud backups by default. If you are storing large or reconstruction-only data (caches, derived data), mark the files to exclude them from backup by setting the NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey resource value on the directory — this is not done automatically by the adapter.

Files are placed in Context.getFilesDir(), the app-internal private storage area. No filesystem permissions are required (no READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE or WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE). androidx.security:security-crypto 1.1.0 (stable) is required for v2.6.0 — this dependency is used by the Secure adapter, not the Filesystem adapter, but both live in the same Gradle build. The Filesystem adapter itself stores values as plain JSON without additional OS-level encryption. For sensitive data, use the Secure adapter instead.

The Filesystem adapter is most practical for values that are too large for Preferences (intended for small values) or that map naturally to a single file — think cached API responses, user-generated drafts, or exported reports. async function cacheApiResponse(endpoint: string, data: unknown) { // Use a hash of the endpoint as the key to avoid filesystem-illegal chars const key = `cache_${btoa(endpoint).replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, '_')}`; await storage.set(key, data, { storage: 'filesystem', ttl: 3_600_000, // 1 hour }); }

class DocumentStore { async save(id: string, content: string) { await storage.set(`doc_${id}`, { content, savedAt: Date.now() }, { storage: 'filesystem', }); } async list(): Promise<string[]> { const keys = await storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'filesystem' }); return keys.filter(k => k.startsWith('doc_')).map(k => k.slice(4)); } }

No sub-directory hierarchy — all files sit in a flat strata_storage/ directory. Slashes in key names are sanitised to underscores; there is no nested folder structure per key. No transactions — unlike SQLite, concurrent writes to the same key can race. Use the adapter only from a single execution context at a time or add your own lock. Slower than SQLite for many small keys — each key requires a separate file I/O round-trip. For high-frequency reads/writes of small values, prefer the SQLite adapter. Not available in browser — isAvailable() returns false outside a Capacitor runtime.
Storage Adapters Overview SQLite Adapter — better choice for many small key-value pairs Platform Guide — iOS Platform Guide — Android Device Verification Guide
Store small app settings in native iOS and Android preferences through Capacitor.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor'; const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'myapp' }); await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage); await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'preferences' }); const theme = await storage.get<string>('theme', { storage: 'preferences' }); Call registerCapacitorAdapters in a native Capacitor app before the first native storage operation. The registration helper returns without registering native adapters in a browser.

StrataConfig.adapters.preferences accepts a boolean. It does not expose an App Group, key prefix, or iCloud sync option. Use the instance namespace to separate logical key groups. const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'settings', defaultStorages: ['preferences', 'memory'], adapters: { preferences: true }, }); await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage); For larger records, use the SQLite adapter or Filesystem adapter. Use the Secure adapter for sensitive values.
Native read, write, persistence, and availability still require iOS and Android device checks. See the device verification guide.
Store sensitive values through Strata Storage's native secure adapter in a Capacitor app.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor'; const storage = defineStorage(); await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage); await storage.set('session_token', token, { storage: 'secure', ttl: 3_600_000, }); const savedToken = await storage.get<string>('session_token', { storage: 'secure' }); await storage.remove('session_token', { storage: 'secure' }); Call registerCapacitorAdapters before the first native operation. It registers no native adapter when running in a browser.

StrataConfig.adapters.secure accepts a boolean. Per-operation StorageOptions supports storage, ttl, encrypt, and other common Strata options. It does not expose Keychain accessibility, a biometric requirement, or an authentication prompt. Do not rely on this adapter for a biometric confirmation flow. Treat the stored values as credentials: keep keys scoped to the application, use a short TTL where appropriate, and remove them at sign-out. Native behavior and persistence need iOS and Android device verification; see the device verification guide.
Capacitor platform guide Encryption guide

The optional Capacitor SQLite adapter stores Strata key/value records in a native SQLite database on iOS and Android. Strata's public API remains key/value based: it does not expose raw SQL, indexes or atomic SQL transactions through storage.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { SqliteAdapter } from 'strata-storage/capacitor'; const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['sqlite'] }); storage.registerAdapter(new SqliteAdapter()); await storage.refreshAdapters(); await storage.set('user:1', { age: 32, city: 'Lahore' }, { storage: 'sqlite', }); const user = await storage.get<{ age: number; city: string }>('user:1', { storage: 'sqlite', }); This needs a running Capacitor iOS or Android app and a synced native project. It cannot prove a native read from a browser tab. Repeat the read after app restart and follow the device verification guide.

SqliteAdapter accepts database and table constructor options. Use distinct instances when different domains need different physical stores: const settings = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['sqlite'] }); settings.registerAdapter(new SqliteAdapter({ database: 'settings', table: 'preferences', })); await settings.refreshAdapters(); await settings.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'sqlite' }); Database and table identifiers are validated. Do not pass arbitrary user input as either name. The native implementation's multi-store and value-wrapper changes still require the project device matrix before a production claim.

storage.query() checks fields of the value returned by get(). It does not query the physical key, Strata wrapper metadata, or a value.* path: const adultsInLahore = await storage.query<{ age: number; city: string }>({ age: { $gte: 18 }, city: 'Lahore', }, { storage: 'sqlite' }); To find keys by name, use storage.keys(/^user:/, { storage: 'sqlite' }). For a pending record, store syncStatus inside the value and query { syncStatus: 'pending' }. Querying through Strata reads and evaluates decoded records; it is not a native indexed SQL query. If your app needs indexed SQL queries, use a native database API directly.

SqliteAdapter.size(true) returns a byte breakdown for keys, values and metadata in the native implementation. Numbers depend on the actual records and platform. Strata's TTL makes expired values read as missing, and cleanupExpired() can reclaim them. Verify these behaviours on the target device before relying on them.

The adapter exposes a best-effort sequential batch internally; capabilities.transactional is false. A failed later operation does not roll back an earlier committed write. Build an application-level recovery path when several writes must succeed together. The native backend, isolation, expiry and size paths are tracked in device verification. No simulator or physical-device result is claimed by this page.
Store Strata key-value data in the browser Cache API.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ adapters: { cache: { cacheName: 'myapp-data-v1' } }, }); await storage.set('api:/items', { items: ['one', 'two'] }, { storage: 'cache', ttl: 300_000, }); const cached = await storage.get<{ items: string[] }>('api:/items', { storage: 'cache', }); The adapter uses string keys and JSON-serializable values. It serializes data inside Cache API responses; it does not store a Request or Response as the value you receive from storage.get(). Use the browser's Cache API directly when you need HTTP request matching or a Response object.

The current adapter requires window and window.caches. It is available from a supported browser page, not from a service worker global scope. Cache API availability and storage quota depend on the browser and origin. Values expire through Strata's TTL handling; an expired value is not a stale-response fallback. StrataConfig.adapters.cache accepts cacheName. Per-call StorageOptions does not accept Cache API matching flags such as ignoreSearch, ignoreMethod, or ignoreVary. const keys = await storage.keys(/^api:/, { storage: 'cache' }); for (const key of keys) { await storage.remove(key, { storage: 'cache' }); }
Offline support example TTL guide

Store small, non-sensitive values in browser cookies. :::info Shared storage area The adapter defaults to the strata_ cookie-name prefix. It lists and clears only values written in Strata's storage envelope. See key ownership. :::

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ adapters: { cookies: { secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' } }, }); await storage.set('language', 'en', { storage: 'cookies', ttl: 86_400_000, }); const language = await storage.get<string>('language', { storage: 'cookies' }); StrataConfig.adapters.cookies accepts secure and sameSite ('strict', 'lax', or 'none'). These are instance settings, not options to pass to set() or get(). Cookie size is limited by the browser; this adapter reports a 4 KB per-cookie limit. To set a domain or path, create and register a CookieAdapter directly: import { Strata, CookieAdapter } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = new Strata({ defaultStorages: ['cookies'] }); storage.registerAdapter(new CookieAdapter('strata_', { domain: '.example.com', path: '/', secure: true, sameSite: 'lax', })); await storage.initialize(); Cookies written by JavaScript cannot be HttpOnly, so do not store session secrets with this adapter. If a server needs an HttpOnly session cookie, it must send the Set-Cookie header itself.
Storage adapters Configuration
Store structured key-value data in the browser's IndexedDB database.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ adapters: { indexedDB: { dbName: 'MyAppDB', version: 1 }, }, }); await storage.set('draft:123', { title: 'First draft' }, { storage: 'indexedDB', }); const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft:123', { storage: 'indexedDB', }); StrataConfig.adapters.indexedDB accepts dbName and version. Its store layout is managed by the adapter. It does not accept a custom object-store schema, an upgrade callback, or an onBlocked callback.

await storage.set('draft:124', { title: 'Second draft' }, { storage: 'indexedDB', ttl: 86_400_000, }); const draftKeys = await storage.keys(/^draft:/, { storage: 'indexedDB', }); for (const key of draftKeys) { const value = await storage.get(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); // Use the value in your application. } The Strata instance exposes no transaction() method. Sequential set() calls do not make an atomic group. For atomic updates across several records, custom indexes, or blocked-upgrade events, use the browser IndexedDB API directly. IndexedDB quotas and persistent-storage decisions are browser controlled. Applications can inspect navigator.storage.estimate() and request persistence with navigator.storage.persist() where supported.
Storage adapters Query guide
Persistent browser storage using the localStorage API.
The LocalStorage adapter provides simple, synchronous, persistent storage in web browsers. Data persists across browser sessions and page reloads.

Feature Support Persistence ✅ Yes Synchronous ✅ Yes Observable ✅ Yes (same origin) Searchable ✅ Yes Iterable ✅ Yes Capacity Varies by browser and available device storage Performance 🚀 Fast TTL Support ✅ Yes (manual) Batch Support ✅ Yes Transaction Support ❌ No

localStorage is shared with every other script on the origin. Since 3.0.0, this adapter prefixes keys with strata: by default. Set keyPrefix: false only when another script must read the exact physical key; older unprefixed keys can migrate on read. Since 2.9.0 the adapter identifies its own data by shape: a key counts as its own only when the stored value deserializes into a StorageValue envelope. Everything else is skipped. What that means in practice: keys() returns only keys this library wrote. A key put in localStorage by anything else is invisible to it by design. The TTL sweep and clear() never read, delete, or log about another application's data. A value that is not ours is not an error — it is evidence the key belongs to somebody else. It is skipped and reported at debug. logger.error is reserved for a key carrying our own envelope that still fails, and for a genuine storage-access fault such as a blocked origin. import { setLogLevel } from 'strata-storage'; setLogLevel('debug'); // names every skipped key and why :::note Before 2.9.0 An empty prefix made the adapter claim every key on the origin. It logged Failed to get key <foreign-key> from localStorage: SyntaxError… on every TTL sweep, returned foreign keys from keys(), and could delete a foreign key whose JSON happened to carry an expired expires. Setting a prefix or a namespace is still good practice for a clean keyspace — it is no longer what keeps the library off other people's keys. :::
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); // Explicitly use localStorage await storage.set('preference', value, { storage: 'localStorage' });
const storage = defineStorage({ adapters: { localStorage: { prefix: 'myapp_' } } });

prefix (string): This adapter's physical-key prefix. The instance-level keyPrefix defaults to strata: and can be set to false for a known external reader; an adapter prefix overrides it. The adapter still identifies its own stored values by their envelope shape.
// Changes are synchronized across tabs storage.subscribe((change) => { if (change.source === 'remote') { console.log(`Tab updated ${change.key}`); } }, { storage: 'localStorage' });
// Data persists for the domain await storage.set('userData', user, { storage: 'localStorage' }); // Available after browser restart
// LocalStorage operations are synchronous under the hood // But Strata wraps them in promises for consistency const value = await storage.get('key', { storage: 'localStorage' });

class PreferenceManager { async saveTheme(theme: 'light' | 'dark') { await storage.set('theme', theme, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } async getTheme() { return await storage.get<'light' | 'dark'>('theme', { storage: 'localStorage' }) || 'light'; } async saveLanguage(lang: string) { await storage.set('language', lang, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } }

// Auto-save form drafts function setupFormAutosave(formId: string) { const form = document.getElementById(formId); form?.addEventListener('input', async (e) => { const formData = new FormData(form as HTMLFormElement); const data = Object.fromEntries(formData); await storage.set(`draft:${formId}`, data, { storage: 'localStorage', ttl: 604800000 // 7 days }); }); // Restore draft on load const draft = await storage.get(`draft:${formId}`, { storage: 'localStorage' }); if (draft) { // Restore form fields } }

class CartManager { private cartKey = 'shopping_cart'; async addItem(item: CartItem) { const cart = await this.getCart(); cart.items.push(item); cart.updatedAt = Date.now(); await storage.set(this.cartKey, cart, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } async getCart(): Promise<Cart> { const cart = await storage.get<Cart>(this.cartKey, { storage: 'localStorage' }); return cart || { items: [], updatedAt: Date.now() }; } async clearCart() { await storage.remove(this.cartKey, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } }

// Queue actions for offline processing class OfflineQueue { async addAction(action: Action) { const queue = await this.getQueue(); queue.push({ ...action, timestamp: Date.now() }); await storage.set('offline_queue', queue, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } async processQueue() { const queue = await this.getQueue(); for (const action of queue) { try { await this.processAction(action); // Remove processed action } catch (error) { // Keep in queue for retry } } } private async getQueue() { return await storage.get('offline_queue', { storage: 'localStorage' }) || []; } }

Browser storage limits vary by browser, device, origin, private-browsing mode, and current disk space. Treat a quota error as a possible write outcome; do not design around a fixed per-browser capacity.

import { QuotaExceededError } from 'strata-storage'; try { await storage.set('data', largeData, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof QuotaExceededError) { // Only remove data that your application can recreate. await storage.clear({ storage: 'localStorage', prefix: 'cache:', }); await storage.set('data', largeData, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } else { throw error; } }

// LocalStorage is bound to origin (protocol + domain + port) // https://example.com cannot access http://example.com localStorage // example.com:3000 cannot access example.com:3001 localStorage // Use a consistent origin or implement cross-origin communication if (window.location.origin === 'https://app.example.com') { await storage.set('data', value, { storage: 'localStorage' }); }
// Namespace your keys to avoid conflicts const storage = defineStorage({ adapters: { localStorage: { prefix: 'myapp_v1_' } } });

// Version your storage schema const STORAGE_VERSION = 2; async function migrateStorage() { const version = await storage.get('_version', { storage: 'localStorage' }); if (!version || version < STORAGE_VERSION) { // Run migrations if (version === 1) { await migrateV1ToV2(); } await storage.set('_version', STORAGE_VERSION, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } }

// Listen for changes from other tabs window.addEventListener('storage', (e) => { if (e.key?.startsWith('myapp_')) { console.log('Storage changed:', e.key, e.newValue); } }); // Or use Strata's subscription const unsubscribe = storage.subscribe((change) => { console.log('Change detected:', change); }, { storage: 'localStorage' });

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const compressedStorage = defineStorage({ compression: { enabled: true } }); await compressedStorage.set('largeData', data, { storage: 'localStorage', compress: true, }); Compression runs only when the instance has compression.enabled: true; a per-write flag alone does not create the compressor. It may leave a value uncompressed when that value would not get smaller.

// localStorage is synchronous and can block the main thread // For large operations, consider batching const batch = []; for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) { batch.push({ key: `item_${i}`, value: data[i] }); } // Batch write for (const { key, value } of batch) { await storage.set(key, value, { storage: 'localStorage' }); }

// Avoid storing non-serializable values const good = { name: 'John', age: 30, tags: ['user', 'active'] }; const bad = { date: new Date(), // Loses type func: () => {}, // Cannot serialize regex: /pattern/ // Loses type }; // Adapter-level serialize/deserialize callbacks are not part of StrataConfig. // Convert a custom value to a supported data shape before calling set().

Do not store account passwords in any client-side adapter. Browser localStorage is readable by scripts on the origin. A Capacitor app can register the native secure adapter for a device-held credential, but that is not a server authentication session or a browser fallback.

// Validate data before storing function sanitizeUserInput(input: string): string { // Remove potential XSS vectors return input.replace(/<script[^>]*>.*?<\/script>/gi, ''); } await storage.set('userContent', sanitizeUserInput(content), { storage: 'localStorage' });

// Fallback chain when localStorage is not available await storage.set('data', value, { storage: ['localStorage', 'sessionStorage', 'memory'] }); // Check availability if (storage.getAvailableStorageTypes().includes('localStorage')) { // Use localStorage } else { // Use alternative }

// Debug localStorage contents const allKeys = await storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'localStorage' }); for (const key of allKeys) { const value = await storage.get(key, { storage: 'localStorage' }); console.log(key, value); } // Get size information const size = await storage.size(true); console.log('LocalStorage usage:', size.byStorage?.localStorage);
Storage Adapters Overview SessionStorage Adapter - Session-scoped storage IndexedDB Adapter - Large-scale storage Cross-Tab Sync Guide
The memory adapter keeps values in a JavaScript Map. Its values disappear when the page or process is reloaded. Use it for data you can regenerate, short-lived previews and tests.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First pass' }, { storage: 'memory' }); const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft', { storage: 'memory', }); defineStorage() registers memory with the standard browser adapters. A manual new Strata() instance needs a registered MemoryAdapter before use.

const limitedStorage = defineStorage({ adapters: { memory: { maxSize: 50 * 1024 * 1024 } }, }); maxSize is a configured byte limit, not a default allocation or a measured capacity. A write that exceeds it throws; the adapter does not evict old entries. Without a configured limit, available JavaScript heap memory is the practical boundary.

await storage.set('report:1', { tags: ['important'], score: 85, }, { storage: 'memory', ttl: 300_000, }); const matches = await storage.query<{ tags: string[]; score: number }>({ tags: { $in: ['important'] }, score: { $gte: 80 }, }, { storage: 'memory' }); query() matches the decoded value, not Strata's internal metadata. Its condition field names are fields of the value you stored. See the query API for operators. To remove only a key family, use a supported clear filter: await storage.clear({ storage: 'memory', prefix: 'report:' }); Memory reads and writes are synchronous at the adapter level, and Strata also exposes async methods. Performance depends on value size and the surrounding application; measure the actual workload instead of assuming a fixed latency.

Reloading or restarting clears the adapter. A separate tab or process has a separate memory map. The adapter has no atomic transaction API and no automatic eviction policy. Use a persistent adapter when the value must survive a reload.
Session-scoped browser storage using the sessionStorage API.
The SessionStorage adapter provides temporary storage that persists for the duration of the browser tab/window session. Data is cleared when the tab is closed.

Feature Support Persistence 🔄 Session only Synchronous ✅ Yes Observable ✅ Yes (same-tab changes; no cross-tab sync) Searchable ✅ Yes Iterable ✅ Yes Capacity Varies by browser and available device storage Performance 🚀 Fast TTL Support ✅ Yes (manual) Batch Support ✅ Yes Transaction Support ❌ No :::info Shared storage area — key ownership This area is shared with every other script on the origin. Since 3.0.0, the adapter prefixes keys with strata: by default. The adapter has also checked the stored StorageValue envelope since 2.9.0, so keys(), the TTL sweep and clear() never touch data this library did not write. A key written here by anything else is invisible to keys() by design; setLogLevel('debug') shows what is being skipped. Full explanation: Configuration ▸ key ownership. :::
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); // Explicitly use sessionStorage await storage.set('sessionData', data, { storage: 'sessionStorage' });
const storage = defineStorage({ adapters: { sessionStorage: { prefix: 'session_' } } });
prefix (string): Physical key prefix. The instance-level default is strata:; this adapter option overrides it. Serialization callbacks are not part of StrataConfig.

// Each tab has its own sessionStorage // Tab 1 await storage.set('tabId', 'tab1', { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); // Tab 2 (different tab) const tabId = await storage.get('tabId', { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); console.log(tabId); // null - different session

// Data survives page refresh within the same tab await storage.set('formProgress', { step: 3 }, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); // After page refresh (same tab) const progress = await storage.get('formProgress', { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); console.log(progress); // { step: 3 }
// No manual cleanup needed - cleared when tab closes await storage.set('tempData', data, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); // Automatically cleared when user closes the tab

class FormWizard { private currentStep = 1; private formKey = 'wizard_data'; async saveStep(stepData: unknown) { const existing = await this.getFormData(); const updated = { ...existing, [`step${this.currentStep}`]: stepData, currentStep: this.currentStep, lastUpdated: Date.now() }; await storage.set(this.formKey, updated, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); } async getFormData() { return await storage.get(this.formKey, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }) || {}; } async nextStep() { this.currentStep++; await this.saveStep({ step: this.currentStep }); } async submitForm() { const formData = await this.getFormData(); await api.submitForm(formData); // Clear after submission await storage.remove(this.formKey, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); } }

class SessionCart { async addItem(item: CartItem) { const cart = await this.getCart(); cart.items.push(item); cart.sessionId = cart.sessionId || generateSessionId(); await storage.set('session_cart', cart, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); } async getCart() { return await storage.get('session_cart', { storage: 'sessionStorage' }) || { items: [], sessionId: null }; } async convertToUser(userId: string) { const sessionCart = await this.getCart(); // Move to persistent storage await storage.set(`cart:${userId}`, sessionCart, { storage: 'localStorage' }); // Clear session cart await storage.remove('session_cart', { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); } }

Keep only recreatable interface state here, such as the selected tab or an unfinished search. Let your authentication system manage credentials; a value in sessionStorage is readable by scripts on the page and cannot prove that a user is signed in.

class PageStateManager { async saveScrollPosition(page: string) { await storage.set(`scroll:${page}`, { x: window.scrollX, y: window.scrollY, timestamp: Date.now() }, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); } async restoreScrollPosition(page: string) { const position = await storage.get(`scroll:${page}`, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); if (position) { window.scrollTo(position.x, position.y); } } async saveFilters(filters: FilterOptions) { await storage.set('page_filters', filters, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); } async getFilters() { return await storage.get('page_filters', { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); } }

// When duplicating a tab, sessionStorage is copied // Original tab await storage.set('data', { value: 1 }, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); // Duplicated tab starts with same data const data = await storage.get('data', { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); console.log(data); // { value: 1 } // But changes are independent await storage.set('data', { value: 2 }, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); // Original tab still has { value: 1 }

// SessionStorage persists across: // - Page refresh (F5) // - Navigation within same origin // - History back/forward // SessionStorage is cleared when: // - Tab is closed // - Browser is closed // - New tab is opened (even to same URL)

// Good: Temporary form data await storage.set('formDraft', draft, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); // Bad: User preferences (use localStorage) await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'localStorage' // Better choice });

class SessionManager { async getOrCreate(key: string, factory: () => Promise<unknown>) { let value = await storage.get(key, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); if (!value) { value = await factory(); await storage.set(key, value, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); } return value; } } // Usage const sessionId = await sessionManager.getOrCreate( 'sessionId', async () => generateSessionId() );
// Clear recreatable session data explicitly on sign-out. class SecureSession { async logout() { await storage.clear({ storage: 'sessionStorage', prefix: 'session_' }); } }

// Since sessionStorage doesn't sync between tabs, // use localStorage or BroadcastChannel for tab communication class TabCoordinator { async setLeaderTab() { const tabId = generateTabId(); // Store in session await storage.set('tabId', tabId, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); // Announce to other tabs via localStorage await storage.set('activeTab', tabId, { storage: 'localStorage', ttl: 5000 // 5 second heartbeat }); } }

// SessionStorage has same size limits as localStorage // Keep data compact interface CompactSession { id: string; s: number; // start time u: number; // last update d: unknown; // data } // Use short keys for frequently accessed data await storage.set('s', compactSession, { storage: 'sessionStorage' });

// Batch multiple operations const updates = [ { key: 'view1', value: data1 }, { key: 'view2', value: data2 }, { key: 'view3', value: data3 } ]; for (const { key, value } of updates) { await storage.set(key, value, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); }

Do not treat a browser-stored user agent, origin, or expiry field as proof of a valid login. The server must validate its own session or access token on every protected request. Avoid putting reusable credentials in browser storage.

// Be cautious with sensitive data // SessionStorage is accessible via JavaScript // Encryption requires a password supplied separately from browser storage. await storage.set('sensitiveData', data, { storage: 'sessionStorage', encrypt: true, encryptionPassword: sessionKey });

Feature SessionStorage LocalStorage Persistence Tab session Permanent Sharing Tab-specific Domain-wide Capacity Browser-dependent Browser-dependent Use Case Temporary state User preferences Auto-cleanup Yes (tab close) No

// Graceful fallback when sessionStorage unavailable const sessionFallback = ['sessionStorage', 'memory']; await storage.set('data', value, { storage: sessionFallback }); // Detect private browsing mode function hasSessionStorage() { try { const test = '__test__'; sessionStorage.setItem(test, test); sessionStorage.removeItem(test); return true; } catch { return false; } }
Storage Adapters Overview LocalStorage Adapter - Persistent storage Memory Adapter - Non-persistent alternative
Persists state in the page URL — shareable, bookmarkable, reload-surviving UI state.

The URL adapter (URLAdapter, storage type 'url') stores each key as a URL parameter, either in the query string (?strata.tab=pending) or the hash fragment (#strata.tab=pending). It is built for small, serializable UI state that should survive a reload and round-trip through navigation: active tab, filters, pagination, selected entity. Added in 2.5.0. URL access is inherently synchronous, so this adapter works with the synchronous API. It also listens for popstate (query mode) or hashchange (hash mode), so back/forward navigation and manual URL edits notify subscribers as 'remote' changes.

Feature Support Persistence ❌ No (lives only as long as the URL) Synchronous ✅ Yes Observable ✅ Yes (popstate / hashchange) Searchable ✅ Yes (via key scan) Iterable ✅ Yes Capacity ~2 KB practical URL budget Cross-tab ❌ No Encrypted ❌ No Transaction Support ❌ No

The URL adapter is not part of the default web set, so register it explicitly: import { defineStorage, URLAdapter } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); storage.registerAdapter(new URLAdapter()); // Write (no await needed — URL access is synchronous) storage.setSync('tab', 'pending', { storage: 'url' }); storage.setSync('page', 3, { storage: 'url' }); // Read it back, e.g. on reload const tab = storage.getSync<string>('tab', { storage: 'url' }); // The async API works too and delegates to the synchronous core await storage.set('q', 'invoices', { storage: 'url' });

Configure the adapter directly before registering it. StrataConfig.adapters has no url field. import { URLAdapter } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); const url = new URLAdapter(); url.configure({ mode: 'hash', history: 'push' }); storage.registerAdapter(url);

Option Type Default Meaning mode 'query' | 'hash' 'query' Store params in the query string or the hash fragment. prefix string 'strata.' Prefix on every param name to avoid collisions with your own query params. history 'push' | 'replace' 'replace' Add a browser history entry per write, or replace the current entry. maxLength number 2000 Soft warning threshold (chars) for total URL length.

The adapter emits change events when the URL changes from outside your code — browser back/forward, or a user editing the address bar. Subscribe to react to those changes: storage.subscribe((change) => { if (change.key === 'tab') applyTab(change.newValue); }, { storage: 'url' });

Query mode (?strata.tab=...) is shared with the server on every navigation and works well for SSR-readable state. Hash mode (#strata.tab=...) keeps state entirely client-side — the fragment is never sent to the server. import { defineStorage, URLAdapter } from 'strata-storage'; // Choose one mode for an instance. Query is the default. const queryStorage = defineStorage(); queryStorage.registerAdapter(new URLAdapter()); // For fragment state, configure a separate adapter before registration. const hashStorage = defineStorage(); const hashAdapter = new URLAdapter(); hashAdapter.configure({ mode: 'hash' }); hashStorage.registerAdapter(hashAdapter);

function applyFilter(status: string, page: number) { storage.setSync('status', status, { storage: 'url' }); storage.setSync('page', page, { storage: 'url' }); } // On load, restore the filters from the URL so a shared link reproduces the view const status = storage.getSync<string>('status', { storage: 'url' }) ?? 'all'; const page = storage.getSync<number>('page', { storage: 'url' }) ?? 1;

function selectTab(tab: string) { storage.setSync('tab', tab, { storage: 'url' }); } window.addEventListener('load', () => { selectTab(storage.getSync<string>('tab', { storage: 'url' }) ?? 'overview'); });

Documented honestly so you choose the right backend: Length limits. URLs have practical limits (~2000 chars in some browsers and servers). This adapter is for small, simple, serializable state — not bulk data. Writes past maxLength are still performed but logged as a debug warning suggesting a different storage. Server visibility. In 'query' mode the data is sent to the server on every navigation and appears in server/proxy/referrer logs. Use 'hash' mode for client-only state. Never store secrets in the URL in either mode. Browser only. Outside a browser (SSR/Node), isAvailable() returns false and the adapter is skipped. Not durable. State lives only as long as the URL does. It is not persistent storage — pair with localStorage/IndexedDB if the value must outlive the URL. No encryption/compression. Like all backends, encrypt/compress require the async path; for the URL adapter, storing large or sensitive values is discouraged regardless.
Storage Adapters Overview Synchronous API — read/write the URL without await LocalStorage Adapter — durable client-only storage Cookie Adapter — small server-readable storage
Strata Storage provides custom error classes for better error handling and debugging.

Error └── StrataError ├── StorageError ├── NotFoundError ├── QuotaExceededError ├── AdapterNotAvailableError ├── NotSupportedError ├── EncryptionError ├── CompressionError ├── SerializationError ├── IntegrityError ├── ValidationError ├── TransactionError ├── MigrationError └── SyncError Every error class extends StrataError directly — StorageError is a sibling, not a parent of NotFoundError/QuotaExceededError/etc. To catch any library error, use instanceof StrataError.

Base error class for all Strata-specific errors. class StrataError extends Error { constructor(message: string, code: string, details?: unknown); readonly name: string; readonly code: string; readonly details?: unknown; } Every Strata error carries a string code (e.g. 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED', 'NOT_FOUND') and an optional details payload. Example​ try { // Some operation } catch (error) { if (error instanceof StrataError) { console.error('Strata error:', error.message); console.error('Code:', error.code); if (error.details) { console.error('Details:', error.details); } } }

General storage operation errors. class StorageError extends StrataError { constructor(message: string, details?: unknown); } Common Causes​ Storage adapter failures Invalid storage operations General storage system errors

Thrown when a requested item is not found. class NotFoundError extends StrataError { constructor(key: string, details?: unknown); } Example​ try { const value = await storage.get('nonexistent'); if (!value) { throw new NotFoundError('nonexistent'); } } catch (error) { if (error instanceof NotFoundError) { console.log(error.message); // Key 'nonexistent' not found } }

Thrown when storage quota is exceeded. class QuotaExceededError extends StrataError { constructor(message?: string, details?: unknown); } Example​ try { await storage.set('largeData', veryLargeObject); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof QuotaExceededError) { console.error('Storage quota exceeded:', error.message); // Clear old data or use different storage } }

Thrown when a requested storage adapter is not available. class AdapterNotAvailableError extends StrataError { constructor(adapterName: string, details?: unknown); } Example​ try { await storage.set('data', value, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof AdapterNotAvailableError) { console.error(error.message); // Storage adapter 'indexedDB' is not available // Fall back to different storage } }

Thrown when an operation is not supported. class NotSupportedError extends StrataError { constructor(operation: string, adapterName?: string, details?: unknown); } Example​ try { await storage.query({ /* complex query */ }); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof NotSupportedError) { console.error(error.message); } }

Errors related to encryption operations. class EncryptionError extends StrataError { constructor(message?: string, details?: unknown); } Common Causes​ Missing or invalid password Corrupted encrypted data Unsupported encryption algorithm Web Crypto API not available Example​ try { await storage.set('secure', data, { encrypt: true }); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof EncryptionError) { console.error('Encryption failed:', error.message); } }

Errors related to compression operations. class CompressionError extends StrataError { constructor(message?: string, details?: unknown); } Common Causes​ Invalid compressed data Decompression failures Unsupported compression algorithm

Errors during data serialization/deserialization. class SerializationError extends StrataError { constructor(message?: string, details?: unknown); } Common Causes​ Circular references in objects Unsupported data types Corrupted serialized data Example​ const circularObj = { name: 'test' }; circularObj.self = circularObj; try { await storage.set('circular', circularObj); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof SerializationError) { console.error('Cannot serialize circular reference'); } }

Data validation errors. class ValidationError extends StrataError { constructor(message: string, details?: unknown); } Common Causes​ Invalid configuration Invalid query conditions Schema validation failures

Transaction-related errors. class TransactionError extends StrataError { constructor(message?: string, details?: unknown); } Common Causes​ Transaction conflicts Transaction timeouts Rollback failures

Migration operation errors. class MigrationError extends StrataError { constructor(message: string, details?: unknown); } Example​ try { await migrationManager.migrate(adapter, targetVersion); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof MigrationError) { console.error('Migration failed:', error.message); } }

Synchronization errors. class SyncError extends StrataError { constructor(message?: string, details?: unknown); } Common Causes​ BroadcastChannel not available Sync message parsing errors Conflict resolution failures
Type guard for Strata errors. function isStrataError(error: unknown): error is StrataError { return error instanceof StrataError; }

Type guard for quota errors. function isQuotaError(error: unknown): boolean; Returns true for a QuotaExceededError, and also for native browser quota errors detected by name/message (e.g. QuotaExceededError, NS_ERROR_DOM_QUOTA_REACHED, or messages containing "quota").

try { await storage.set('data', value); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof QuotaExceededError) { // Handle quota exceeded await storage.clear({ olderThan: Date.now() - 86400000 }); await storage.set('data', value); // Retry } else if (error instanceof EncryptionError) { // Handle encryption error console.error('Encryption failed, storing unencrypted'); await storage.set('data', value, { encrypt: false }); } else if (error instanceof StrataError) { // Handle any other Strata error console.error('Storage error:', error.message); } else { // Unexpected error throw error; } }

async function saveWithFallback(key: string, value: unknown) { const storageTypes: StorageType[] = ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory']; for (const storage of storageTypes) { try { await storage.set(key, value, { storage }); return storage; } catch (error) { if (error instanceof AdapterNotAvailableError) { continue; // Try next storage } throw error; // Unrecoverable error } } throw new StorageError('No storage available'); }

function logStrataError(error: unknown) { if (error instanceof StrataError) { console.error(`[${error.name}] ${error.message}`); console.error(`Code: ${error.code}`); if (error.details) { console.error('Details:', error.details); } } }

function getUserMessage(error: unknown): string { if (error instanceof QuotaExceededError) { return 'Storage space is full. Please free up some space.'; } else if (error instanceof EncryptionError) { return 'Failed to encrypt data. Please check your password.'; } else if (error instanceof NotFoundError) { return 'The requested item could not be found.'; } else if (error instanceof AdapterNotAvailableError) { return 'Storage is not available in your browser.'; } else if (error instanceof StrataError) { return 'Storage operation failed. Please try again.'; } return 'An unexpected error occurred.'; }

The main class for interacting with Strata Storage.

There are three ways to get a working storage instance. Most apps should use defineStorage() or the default storage singleton — both register the standard web adapters and initialize lazily on first use, so you never have to call initialize() yourself.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage'], }); Returns a ready-to-use Strata instance with memory, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies, and the Cache API pre-registered — the framework-agnostic, Zustand-style entry point. Create it once anywhere and import it everywhere; no Provider is required. It initializes lazily (every operation awaits readiness internally), so you can call get/set/subscribe immediately.

import { storage } from 'strata-storage'; await storage.set('key', 'value'); // works immediately Built from the same factory as defineStorage(). Importing the package performs no I/O — initialization happens on first use. ensureInitialized() is exported if you want to force readiness before a burst of calls (it is optional and idempotent).

import { Strata, MemoryAdapter } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = new Strata({ defaultStorages: ['memory'] }); storage.registerAdapter(new MemoryAdapter()); await storage.initialize(); Use the constructor directly when you want full control over which adapters are registered. registerWebAdapters(strata) is exported to register the same default web set on a custom instance. Parameters​ config (optional): Configuration object. See StrataConfig. New 2.5.0 recovery fields (integrity, durableWrites, mirror, autoBackup) are documented in Recovery & Integrity.

async initialize(): Promise<void> Initializes an instance explicitly. defineStorage() and the exported singleton initialize lazily on first use; manual instances need registered adapters before use. import { Strata, registerWebAdapters } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = registerWebAdapters(new Strata()); await storage.initialize();

async get<T = unknown>(key: string, options?: StorageOptions): Promise<T | null> Retrieves a value from storage. Parameters​ key: The key to retrieve options (optional): Storage options Returns​ The stored value or null if not found Example​ // Simple get const value = await storage.get('username'); // With type const user = await storage.get<User>('currentUser'); // With options const data = await storage.get('data', { storage: 'indexedDB', skipDecryption: false });

async set<T = unknown>( key: string, value: T, options?: StorageOptions ): Promise<void> Stores a value in storage. Parameters​ key: The key to store under value: The value to store options (optional): Storage options Example​ import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); await storage.set('username', 'john_doe'); await storage.set('draft', { status: 'editing' }, { storage: 'indexedDB', ttl: 3_600_000, }); Native secure storage needs Capacitor adapter registration. Encryption and compression need an instance configured for those transforms; see the native setup, encryption and compression guides.

async remove(key: string, options?: StorageOptions): Promise<void> Removes a value from storage. Parameters​ key: The key to remove options (optional): Storage options Example​ await storage.remove('tempData'); await storage.remove('draft', { storage: 'indexedDB' });

async has(key: string, options?: StorageOptions): Promise<boolean> Checks if a key exists in storage. Parameters​ key: The key to check options (optional): Storage options Returns​ true if the key exists, false otherwise Example​ if (await storage.has('authToken')) { // User is authenticated }

async clear(options?: ClearOptions & StorageOptions): Promise<void> Clears storage data. Parameters​ options (optional): Clear and storage options Example​ // Clear all storage await storage.clear(); // Clear specific storage await storage.clear({ storage: 'localStorage' }); // Clear with filters (ClearOptions: storage, namespace, prefix, pattern, tags, olderThan, expiredOnly) await storage.clear({ prefix: 'temp_', // only keys starting with 'temp_' olderThan: Date.now() - 86400000 // and created over 24 hours ago });

async keys( pattern?: string | RegExp, options?: StorageOptions ): Promise<string[]> Gets all keys, optionally filtered by pattern. Parameters​ pattern (optional): String or RegExp pattern to filter keys options (optional): Storage options Returns​ Array of matching keys Example​ // Get all keys const allKeys = await storage.keys(); // Filter by prefix const userKeys = await storage.keys('user_'); // Filter by regex const tempKeys = await storage.keys(/^temp_.*$/);

For UI code that must read or write without await, Strata mirrors the core operations synchronously. Added in 2.5.0. getSync<T = unknown>(key: string, options?: StorageOptions): T | null setSync<T = unknown>(key: string, value: T, options?: StorageOptions): void removeSync(key: string, options?: StorageOptions): void hasSync(key: string, options?: StorageOptions): boolean keysSync(pattern?: string | RegExp, options?: StorageOptions): string[] clearSync(options?: ClearOptions & StorageOptions): void These work only on synchronous adapters: memory, localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, and url. With no explicit storage, keysSync/clearSync aggregate across the sync-capable adapters. The lookup falls back to the registry, so sync calls work even before async initialize() has completed. storage.setSync('lastTab', 'inbox'); const tab = storage.getSync<string>('lastTab'); // 'inbox' storage.setSync('filters', { status: 'open' }, { storage: 'localStorage', ttl: 60_000 }); storage.keysSync(); // string[] across memory/localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies/url storage.clearSync(); Constraints​ Targeting an async-only adapter (indexedDB, cache, sqlite, filesystem, secure, preferences) throws a StorageError — use the async API instead. setSync with { encrypt: true } or { compress: true } throws: encryption and compression are inherently asynchronous. Use await storage.set(...). getSync on a value that was stored encrypted or compressed throws. Read it with await storage.get(...). TTL, tags, and metadata are supported by the synchronous API.

Adopt ONE foreign localStorage / sessionStorage entry, named by its exact physical key, into a Strata key, and delete the original. It is the migration path for data written by something other than this library (a raw localStorage.setItem, a pre-Strata zustand store), which the implicit legacy-key migration deliberately never adopts. Added in 3.1.0. importRawSync(rawKey: string, key: string, options?: StorageOptions): string | null // Before: the app wrote localStorage.setItem('app-theme', 'dark') itself. storage.importRawSync('app-theme', 'app-theme', { storage: 'localStorage' }); // 'dark' storage.getSync<string>('app-theme', { storage: 'localStorage' }); // 'dark' The raw string is kept as-is (it is not parsed). It returns the adopted string, or null when there was nothing to adopt or key already holds a value. An existing value at key wins, and nothing is moved. Only localStorage and sessionStorage can import. Any other adapter throws a StorageError. The source is removed only after the destination write succeeds. Since 3.1.1, when keyPrefix: false makes the source and destination the same physical key, the newly written envelope is kept (ISSUE-14).

async size(detailed?: boolean): Promise<SizeInfo> Gets storage size information. Parameters​ detailed (optional): Include detailed breakdown Returns​ Size information object Example​ const size = await storage.size(); console.log(`Total: ${size.total} bytes, Items: ${size.count}`); const detailed = await storage.size(true); console.log('By storage:', detailed.byStorage);

async query<T = unknown>( condition: QueryCondition, options?: StorageOptions & QueryOptions ): Promise<Array<{ key: string; value: T }>> Queries storage with advanced conditions. Conditions match the decoded value using bare field names (e.g. { age: { $gte: 18 } }); wrapper fields like key, tags, created, and expires are not queryable. See the Query API for the full model and operators ($eq $ne $gt $gte $lt $lte $in $nin $regex $exists $type $and $or $not). Parameters​ condition: Query conditions matched against the stored value options (optional): Storage options plus query options (sort, skip, limit, select) Returns​ Array of matching key-value pairs Example​ // Query by a value field const admins = await storage.query({ role: 'admin' }); // Range query on a value field const adults = await storage.query({ age: { $gte: 18 } }); // Complex query — bare value fields + logical operators const results = await storage.query({ $and: [ { status: 'active' }, { score: { $gte: 10 } } ] });

subscribe( callback: SubscriptionCallback, options?: StorageOptions ): UnsubscribeFunction Subscribes to storage changes. Parameters​ callback: Function called on storage changes options (optional): Storage options Returns​ Function to unsubscribe Example​ const unsubscribe = storage.subscribe((change) => { console.log(`Key ${change.key} changed`); console.log('Old value:', change.oldValue); console.log('New value:', change.newValue); }); // Later... unsubscribe(); Which backends actually deliver​ Omitting options attaches to every registered adapter that can emit change events — memory, localStorage, sessionStorage and url. indexedDB, cookies and cache have no native change notification and are skipped, so an unscoped subscription hears fewer backends than are registered. That is the intended outcome: an observer that hears everything able to speak. Naming a non-observable backend explicitly logs a warning, because a subscription that can never fire is almost certainly not what you meant: storage.subscribe(cb, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); // [strata-storage] subscribe: storage "indexedDB" does not support change events, // so this subscription will never fire. :::note Before 2.9.0 The unscoped form threw NotSupportedError: Operation 'subscribe' is not supported by indexedDB adapter, because the fan-out did not skip backends that cannot subscribe — and indexedDB is registered on every default instance. Since the throw propagated out of whatever set up the subscription, it commonly took application boot down with it. Scoping to { storage: 'localStorage' } was the workaround; it still works and is tighter when only one backend matters. :::

async export(options?: ExportOptions): Promise<string> Exports storage data. Parameters​ options (optional): Export options Returns​ Exported data as string Example​ // Export all data const backup = await storage.export(); // Export specific keys const userData = await storage.export({ keys: ['user', 'preferences', 'settings'], format: 'json', pretty: true });

async import(data: string, options?: ImportOptions): Promise<void> Imports storage data. Parameters​ data: Data to import options (optional): Import options Example​ // Import with overwrite await storage.import(backupData, { format: 'json', overwrite: true }); // Import with merge await storage.import(partialData, { merge: 'shallow' });

async snapshot(options?: ExportOptions): Promise<string> Creates a portable, integrity-verified backup of all stored data. Added in 2.5.0. The returned string embeds a manifest (version, timestamp, FNV-1a checksum, and the full export including metadata) so restore() can detect a corrupted backup. Pair with config.autoBackup for scheduled snapshots. Returns​ A JSON string containing the checksum manifest and payload. Example​ const backup = await storage.snapshot(); // Persist `backup` to a file, server, or another storage type.

async restore(snapshot: string, options?: ImportOptions): Promise<void> Restores data from a snapshot() string. Added in 2.5.0. Validates the manifest checksum and throws IntegrityError if the backup is corrupted. A plain export string (no manifest) is also accepted and imported directly. Snapshot payloads are written back with their full value wrappers intact, preserving TTL, tags, encryption flags, and checksums. Parameters​ snapshot: A string produced by snapshot() (or a raw export() string) options (optional): Import options Example​ try { await storage.restore(backup); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof IntegrityError) { // The backup is corrupted — checksum mismatch. } } See Recovery & Integrity for the full recovery toolkit (integrity, durable writes, mirroring, auto-backup).

async getTTL(key: string, options?: StorageOptions): Promise<number | null> Gets time-to-live for a key. Parameters​ key: The key to check options (optional): Storage options Returns​ Milliseconds until expiration or null if no TTL Example​ const ttl = await storage.getTTL('sessionToken'); if (ttl && ttl < 60000) { // Token expires in less than 1 minute await refreshToken(); }

async extendTTL( key: string, extension: number, options?: StorageOptions ): Promise<void> Extends the TTL of a key. Parameters​ key: The key to extend extension: Milliseconds to add to current TTL options (optional): Storage options Example​ // Extend by 1 hour await storage.extendTTL('session', 3600000);

async persist(key: string, options?: StorageOptions): Promise<void> Makes a key persistent (removes TTL). Parameters​ key: The key to persist options (optional): Storage options Example​ await storage.persist('importantData');

async getExpiring( timeWindow: number, options?: StorageOptions ): Promise<Array<{ key: string; expiresIn: number }>> Gets items expiring within a time window. Parameters​ timeWindow: Milliseconds to look ahead options (optional): Storage options Returns​ Array of expiring items Example​ // Get items expiring in next hour const expiring = await storage.getExpiring(3600000); for (const item of expiring) { console.log(`${item.key} expires in ${item.expiresIn}ms`); }

async cleanupExpired(options?: StorageOptions): Promise<number> Manually triggers cleanup of expired items. Parameters​ options (optional): Storage options Returns​ Number of items removed Example​ const removed = await storage.cleanupExpired(); console.log(`Cleaned up ${removed} expired items`);

generatePassword(length?: number): string Generates a secure random password. Parameters​ length (optional): Password length (default: 32) Returns​ Generated password Example​ const password = storage.generatePassword(16);
async hash(data: string): Promise<string> Hashes data using SHA-256. Parameters​ data: Data to hash Returns​ Hex-encoded hash Example​ const hash = await storage.hash('sensitive-data');

getAvailableStorageTypes(): StorageType[] Gets list of available storage types. Returns​ Array of available storage type names Example​ const types = storage.getAvailableStorageTypes(); // ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'sessionStorage', 'memory']

getCapabilities(storage?: StorageType): StorageCapabilities | Record<string, StorageCapabilities> Gets capabilities of storage adapters. Parameters​ storage (optional): Specific storage type Returns​ Capabilities object or map of all capabilities Example​ // Get specific adapter capabilities const indexedDBCaps = storage.getCapabilities('indexedDB'); // Get all capabilities const allCaps = storage.getCapabilities();
async close(): Promise<void> Closes all storage connections and cleans up resources. Example​ // Clean shutdown await storage.close();
These are module-level exports (not static methods on the class).

function defineStorage(config?: StrataConfig): Strata Creates a Strata instance with the standard web adapters pre-registered. The recommended entry point — see Creating an instance. import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true, password: '…' } });

function registerWebAdapters(strata: Strata): Strata Registers memory, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies, and Cache API adapters on an existing instance and returns it for chaining. Used internally by defineStorage(); call it directly to add the default web set to a new Strata(...) you configured yourself.
function ensureInitialized(): Promise<void> Forces initialization of the default storage singleton and awaits readiness. Optional (every operation auto-awaits readiness) and idempotent.
The Strata class emits events through the subscription system: set - When a value is set remove - When a value is removed clear - When storage is cleared expire - When an item expires

All async methods can throw errors. See Error Classes for details. import { StorageError, QuotaExceededError } from 'strata-storage'; try { await storage.set('data', largeData); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof QuotaExceededError) { // Handle quota exceeded } else if (error instanceof StorageError) { // Handle other storage errors } }
