Strata Storage is a local key/value layer, not an analytics provider. You can use it to hold a small event outbox until your own endpoint accepts the events. Collect only after the user has given the consent your product requires, and keep sensitive values out of event properties. Record an event Replay the outbox Query and clear local records

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'analytics-example' }); type PageEvent = { id: string; name: 'page_view'; path: string; occurredAt: number; }; async function trackPageView(hasConsent: boolean): Promise<void> { if (!hasConsent) return; const event: PageEvent = { id: crypto.randomUUID(), name: 'page_view', path: window.location.pathname, occurredAt: Date.now(), }; await storage.set(`event:${event.id}`, event, { storage: 'indexedDB', ttl: 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000, }); } The event stores a path, not the full URL with query parameters. The 7-day TTL bounds the local queue; an event that expires before delivery is lost. Choose retention from your product's privacy policy and operational needs.

async function sendPendingEvents(): Promise<void> { const keys = await storage.keys(/^event:/, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); for (const key of keys) { const event = await storage.get<PageEvent>(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); if (!event) continue; try { const response = await fetch('/api/analytics', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Idempotency-Key': event.id, }, body: JSON.stringify(event), }); if (response.ok) await storage.remove(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); } catch { // Keep the event for a later attempt. } } } /api/analytics is your own endpoint. It must validate the event, enforce consent and deduplicate the operation ID before accepting it. A failed HTTP status leaves the event queued. Aggregate counts and charts on the server; a client-side scan of local events cannot represent all users.

const docsViews = await storage.query<PageEvent>({ name: 'page_view', path: '/docs', }, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); // When consent is withdrawn, stop tracking and clear this local outbox. await storage.clear({ storage: 'indexedDB', prefix: 'event:' }); query() matches name and path because both fields are in the stored value. The result is this browser's local records only. If your app sends events to other providers too, consent withdrawal must cover those paths as well.

An Angular service can own one Strata instance and expose the operations your components need. This example keeps small drafts in browser localStorage, whose adapter emits change events. It doesn't implement authentication or a shared server database. Draft service Subscriptions and limits

import { Injectable } from '@angular/core'; import { defineStorage, type StorageChange } from 'strata-storage'; type Draft = { title: string; status: 'open' | 'closed'; }; @Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' }) export class DraftStorageService { private readonly storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'angular-drafts', defaultStorages: ['localStorage'], }); async save(id: string, draft: Draft): Promise<void> { await this.storage.set(`draft:${id}`, draft, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } async load(id: string): Promise<Draft | null> { return this.storage.get<Draft>(`draft:${id}`, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } async remove(id: string): Promise<void> { await this.storage.remove(`draft:${id}`, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } async listOpen(): Promise<Array<{ key: string; value: Draft }>> { return this.storage.query<Draft>({ status: 'open' }, { storage: 'localStorage', }); } subscribe(onChange: (change: StorageChange) => void): () => void { return this.storage.subscribe(change => { if (change.key.startsWith('draft:')) onChange(change); }, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } } Inject DraftStorageService into a component, call its async methods and show a pending or failure state around writes. load() returns null for a missing draft. The service uses only public methods; it never reaches into a private .storage field from another class.

subscribe() returns an unsubscribe function. A component that registers a callback should call it when the component is destroyed. The localStorage adapter emits local writes and browser storage events from other tabs. The indexedDB adapter does not advertise change observation, so don't move this subscription to IndexedDB and assume it will fire. query() scans decoded local values. Keep the namespace dedicated to drafts, or add a value field to distinguish records. For large datasets, let your server query and aggregate the records.
Simple examples to get started with Strata Storage.
npm install strata-storage # or yarn add strata-storage

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); // Store data await storage.set('user_name', 'John Doe'); await storage.set('user_age', 30); await storage.set('user_preferences', { theme: 'dark', language: 'en', notifications: true }); // Retrieve data const name = await storage.get('user_name'); console.log(name); // 'John Doe' const preferences = await storage.get('user_preferences'); console.log(preferences); // { theme: 'dark', ... }
// Remove single item await storage.remove('user_age'); // Clear all data await storage.clear();

// Check if key exists const exists = await storage.has('user_name'); console.log(exists); // true or false // Get all keys const keys = await storage.keys(); console.log(keys); // ['user_name', 'user_preferences', ...]

// Use specific storage await storage.set('session_data', data, { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); await storage.set('persistent_data', data, { storage: 'localStorage' }); await storage.set('large_data', data, { storage: 'indexedDB' });

// Data expires in 1 hour await storage.set('temp_token', token, { ttl: 3600000 // milliseconds }); // Data expires at specific time await storage.set('daily_cache', data, { expireAt: new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) });

// Store complex objects const user = { id: 123, name: 'John Doe', email: 'john@example.com', roles: ['user', 'admin'], metadata: { lastLogin: new Date(), loginCount: 42 } }; await storage.set('current_user', user); // Retrieve and use const savedUser = await storage.get('current_user'); console.log(savedUser.roles); // ['user', 'admin']

// Store ArrayBuffer const buffer = new ArrayBuffer(256); await storage.set('binary_data', buffer); // Store Blob const blob = new Blob(['Hello World'], { type: 'text/plain' }); await storage.set('file_blob', blob); // Store Uint8Array const bytes = new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]); await storage.set('byte_array', bytes);

try { await storage.set('key', 'value'); } catch (error) { if (error.code === 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED') { console.error('Storage quota exceeded'); } else { console.error('Storage error:', error); } } // Safe get with default value const value = await storage.get('maybe_missing') || 'default';

// Set multiple values const items = { 'user:1': { name: 'Alice' }, 'user:2': { name: 'Bob' }, 'user:3': { name: 'Charlie' } }; for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(items)) { await storage.set(key, value); } // Get multiple values const userIds = ['user:1', 'user:2', 'user:3']; const users = []; for (const id of userIds) { const user = await storage.get(id); if (user) users.push(user); }

// Create namespaced storage const userStorage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'users' }); const appStorage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'app' }); // Data is isolated await userStorage.set('data', 'user data'); await appStorage.set('data', 'app data'); const userData = await userStorage.get('data'); // 'user data' const appData = await appStorage.get('data'); // 'app data'

// Browser storage; native adapters need explicit registration const storage = defineStorage(); // On web: prefers localStorage, then IndexedDB, sessionStorage and memory. // On iOS/Android: register native adapters before selecting them. // See the Capacitor platform guide for device setup. await storage.set('cross_platform', 'Works everywhere!');

Learn how to perform Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations with Strata Storage.
Setup Create (Set) Read (Get) Update Delete (Remove) List Operations Multiple Items Error Handling
First, create a web-ready instance. It initializes on the first operation: import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage();
// String await storage.set('username', 'john_doe'); // Number await storage.set('age', 25); // Boolean await storage.set('isActive', true); // Null await storage.set('optionalValue', null);
await storage.set('user', { id: 123, name: 'John Doe', email: 'john@example.com', age: 25 });
await storage.set('favoriteColors', ['red', 'blue', 'green']); await storage.set('users', [ { id: 1, name: 'John' }, { id: 2, name: 'Jane' } ]);

// Specify storage adapter await storage.set('largeData', bigObject, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); // With TTL (expires in 1 hour) await storage.set('sessionData', data, { ttl: 60 * 60 * 1000 }); // Enable encryption on a separate instance before asking it to encrypt. const encryptedStorage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true } }); await encryptedStorage.set('sensitiveData', secret, { encryptionPassword: password }); // Compression also needs instance configuration. const compressedStorage = defineStorage({ compression: { enabled: true } }); await compressedStorage.set('hugeData', massiveObject); // With tags for querying await storage.set('document', content, { tags: ['work', 'important', '2024'] });

const username = await storage.get('username'); console.log(username); // 'john_doe' const age = await storage.get('age'); console.log(age); // 25 const isActive = await storage.get('isActive'); console.log(isActive); // true

const user = await storage.get('user'); console.log(user); // { id: 123, name: 'John Doe', email: 'john@example.com', age: 25 } // Access properties console.log(user.name); // 'John Doe' console.log(user.email); // 'john@example.com'

const colors = await storage.get('favoriteColors'); console.log(colors); // ['red', 'blue', 'green'] const users = await storage.get('users'); console.log(users); // [{ id: 1, name: 'John' }, { id: 2, name: 'Jane' }]

// If key doesn't exist, returns null const theme = await storage.get('theme'); console.log(theme); // null // Use || for default value const themeWithDefault = await storage.get('theme') || 'light'; console.log(themeWithDefault); // 'light' // Use ?? for null coalescing const language = await storage.get('language') ?? 'en'; console.log(language); // 'en'
interface User { id: number; name: string; email: string; } const user = await storage.get<User>('user'); if (user) { // TypeScript knows user is User console.log(user.name); // Type-safe }
// Get from specific storage const data = await storage.get('key', { storage: 'indexedDB' });
// Original await storage.set('user', { id: 1, name: 'John', age: 25 }); // Update (replaces entire object) await storage.set('user', { id: 1, name: 'John Doe', age: 26 });
// Get current value const user = await storage.get('user'); // Modify user.age = 27; user.email = 'newemail@example.com'; // Save back await storage.set('user', user);
const user = await storage.get('user'); // Update specific properties await storage.set('user', { ...user, age: 28, lastUpdated: new Date() });

// Add item to array const colors = await storage.get('favoriteColors') || []; colors.push('yellow'); await storage.set('favoriteColors', colors); // Remove item from array const users = await storage.get('users') || []; const filteredUsers = users.filter(u => u.id !== 2); await storage.set('users', filteredUsers); // Update array item const items = await storage.get('items') || []; const updatedItems = items.map(item => item.id === 3 ? { ...item, status: 'completed' } : item ); await storage.set('items', updatedItems);

// Increment counter const count = await storage.get('counter') || 0; await storage.set('counter', count + 1); // Decrement const score = await storage.get('score') || 100; await storage.set('score', score - 10);
await storage.remove('username'); // Verify deletion const username = await storage.get('username'); console.log(username); // null

await storage.remove('username'); await storage.remove('age'); await storage.remove('isActive'); // For a list of keys, wait for every removal await Promise.all(['username', 'age', 'isActive'].map((key) => storage.remove(key)));
// Remove everything await storage.clear(); // Verify const keys = await storage.keys(); console.log(keys); // []
// Clear only localStorage await storage.clear({ storage: 'localStorage' }); // Clear only indexedDB await storage.clear({ storage: 'indexedDB' });
// Remove items matching condition const allKeys = await storage.keys(); for (const key of allKeys) { if (key.startsWith('temp_')) { await storage.remove(key); } }
const keys = await storage.keys(); console.log(keys); // ['username', 'user', 'settings', ...]

const keys = await storage.keys(); const allData = Object.fromEntries(await Promise.all( keys.map(async (key) => [key, await storage.get(key)]) )); console.log(allData); // { // username: 'john_doe', // user: { id: 123, name: 'John' }, // settings: { theme: 'dark' } // }
const hasUsername = await storage.has('username'); console.log(hasUsername); // true const hasUnknown = await storage.has('nonexistent'); console.log(hasUnknown); // false
const size = await storage.size(); console.log(`Storage contains ${size.count} items`); console.log(`Storage uses approximately ${size.total} bytes`);
These calls run independently. If one fails, earlier writes may already have succeeded.
await Promise.all([ storage.set('username', 'john_doe'), storage.set('email', 'john@example.com'), storage.set('age', 25) ]);

const keys = ['username', 'email', 'age']; const values = Object.fromEntries(await Promise.all( keys.map(async (key) => [key, await storage.get(key)]) )); console.log(values); // { // username: 'john_doe', // email: 'john@example.com', // age: 25 // }
await Promise.all(['username', 'email', 'age'].map((key) => storage.remove(key)));
await storage.set('user1', data1, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); await storage.set('user2', data2, { encrypt: true, encryptionPassword: password }); await storage.set('user3', data3, { ttl: 3600000 });
try { await storage.set('key', 'value'); } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to set value:', error); }

import { StorageError, QuotaExceededError, StorageNotAvailableError } from 'strata-storage'; try { await storage.set('largeData', hugeObject); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof QuotaExceededError) { console.error('Storage quota exceeded'); // Clear old data or use different adapter await storage.clear(); } else if (error instanceof StorageNotAvailableError) { console.error('Storage not available'); // Use fallback await storage.set('largeData', hugeObject, { storage: 'memory' }); } else if (error instanceof StorageError) { console.error('Storage error:', error.message); } }

// Safely get with default async function safeGet(key: string, defaultValue: any) { try { const value = await storage.get(key); return value ?? defaultValue; } catch (error) { console.error(`Failed to get ${key}:`, error); return defaultValue; } } // Safely set async function safeSet(key: string, value: any) { try { await storage.set(key, value); return true; } catch (error) { console.error(`Failed to set ${key}:`, error); return false; } } // Usage const theme = await safeGet('theme', 'light'); const success = await safeSet('theme', 'dark');

Here's a complete example demonstrating all CRUD operations: import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; async function crudExample() { // Setup const storage = defineStorage(); // CREATE await storage.set('user', { id: 1, name: 'John Doe', email: 'john@example.com', preferences: { theme: 'dark', language: 'en' } }); console.log('User created'); // READ const user = await storage.get('user'); console.log('User data:', user); // UPDATE const updatedUser = { ...user, name: 'John Smith', preferences: { ...user.preferences, theme: 'light' } }; await storage.set('user', updatedUser); console.log('User updated'); // READ AGAIN const currentUser = await storage.get('user'); console.log('Updated user:', currentUser); // LIST const allKeys = await storage.keys(); console.log('All keys:', allKeys); const allData = Object.fromEntries(await Promise.all( allKeys.map(async (key) => [key, await storage.get(key)]) )); console.log('All data:', allData); // DELETE await storage.remove('user'); console.log('User deleted'); // VERIFY const deletedUser = await storage.get('user'); console.log('User after deletion:', deletedUser); // null } // Run the example crudExample();

A cache is useful only when a miss can be recovered. These examples cache JSON data in a browser adapter and let TTL remove stale entries. Strata's Cache adapter stores JSON-serializable key/value data; it is not the browser's Request/Response cache.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'api-cache' }); type Profile = { id: string; name: string }; async function getProfile(id: string): Promise<Profile> { const key = `profile:${id}`; const cached = await storage.get<Profile>(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); if (cached !== null) return cached; const response = await fetch(`/api/profiles/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`); if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Profile request failed'); const profile = await response.json() as Profile; await storage.set(key, profile, { storage: 'indexedDB', ttl: 5 * 60 * 1000, }); return profile; } The endpoint and response shape belong to your application. Validate the server response before trusting it, and show an error if the network read or local write fails. A cached profile can be stale until its TTL expires; choose a TTL appropriate to your data.

await storage.clear({ storage: 'indexedDB', prefix: 'profile:' }); clear() accepts filters such as prefix, pattern and olderThan. It does not accept a callback filter. To inspect keys first, use storage.keys(/^profile:/, { storage: 'indexedDB' }).

A query() result contains { key, value }, not TTL metadata. It cannot report how many stored entries are expired. Track hits and misses in your application if that metric matters. For a byte estimate, storage.size(true) reports adapter totals; test its output on the adapter and runtime you ship rather than assuming a fixed capacity or latency. If you need to cache HTTP Response objects in a service worker, use the browser Cache API directly. Strata's Cache adapter currently requires window and does not run in service-worker scope.

A Capacitor app can use the same set() and get() calls on web, iOS and Android after it registers the native adapters. A browser build exercises the web adapters; native persistence needs device testing.

import { Capacitor } from '@capacitor/core'; import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor'; const native = Capacitor.isNativePlatform(); const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'my-app', defaultStorages: native ? ['sqlite', 'preferences', 'memory'] : ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], }); if (native) await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage); await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First pass' }); const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft'); Create this instance once in the app's startup path and share it with screens. Call registerCapacitorAdapters() before the first native operation.

if (native) { await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'preferences' }); await storage.set('offline-draft', draft, { storage: 'sqlite' }); await storage.set('device-credential', credential, { storage: 'secure' }); } else { await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'localStorage' }); await storage.set('offline-draft', draft, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); } An explicit native storage type is unavailable in a regular browser. Choose a browser fallback for shared code; check native availability and round-trip behavior on both devices.

Strata's secure adapter does not provide a biometric prompt or a biometricOnly option. If the host app needs a biometric check, it must choose and verify a separate authentication mechanism. That check is not a guarantee that a value written through Strata remains biometric-gated on later reads.

import { App } from '@capacitor/app'; const listener = await App.addListener('appStateChange', async ({ isActive }) => { if (!isActive) { await storage.set('lastPauseAt', Date.now(), { storage: native ? 'preferences' : 'localStorage', }); } }); // Remove the listener when the app shell is disposed. await listener.remove(); Use the device verification guide to test restart persistence and each adapter. An app state event is not a substitute for awaiting a write when data must be durable.
Capacitor platform guide Native adapter reference
Strata's bundled LZ codec runs when the instance has compression.enabled: true. A compress: true option on an unconfigured instance does not initialize the compressor.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ compression: { enabled: true } }); await storage.set('large-dataset', largeData, { compress: true }); const restored = await storage.get('large-dataset'); Compression and decompression use the async API.

const storage = defineStorage({ compression: { enabled: true, threshold: 1024, algorithm: 'lz', }, }); await storage.set('user-list', largeUserArray); await storage.set('small-config', { theme: 'dark' }); The configured threshold decides whether the data is large enough to compress. Compression may not reduce every value's size.

const storage = defineStorage({ compression: { enabled: true } }); await storage.set('api-response', jsonData, { compress: true }); await storage.set('small-config', { theme: 'dark' }, { compress: false }); To combine compression and encryption, enable both features on the instance and supply an encryption password. Strata compresses before encrypting: const storage = defineStorage({ compression: { enabled: true }, encryption: { enabled: true }, }); await storage.set('private-draft', draft, { compress: true, encrypt: true, encryptionPassword: password, });

CompressionManager.compress() returns compression output for the value you pass it; it does not report a database-wide saved-byte total. Measure a representative input and the actual stored payload if your application needs a size comparison.
const storage = defineStorage({ compression: { enabled: true } }); const shouldCompress = JSON.stringify(value).length >= 1024; await storage.set('result', value, { compress: shouldCompress });
Rewriting all existing keys changes their stored representation and expiry metadata. Migrate a bounded, known key set only after testing a read-write-read round-trip and any TTL requirements.
Compression guide Configuration
Use defineStorage() for a web-ready instance. It registers the standard web adapters and initializes on the first operation.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'my-app', defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], debug: { enabled: true, verbosity: 'normal' }, }); await storage.set('theme', 'dark');

const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'my-app', defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], adapters: { indexedDB: { dbName: 'MyAppDB', version: 1 }, localStorage: { prefix: 'myapp:' }, }, compression: { enabled: true, threshold: 1024, algorithm: 'lz' }, ttl: { cleanupInterval: 60_000, defaultTTL: 3_600_000 }, sync: { enabled: true, storages: ['localStorage', 'indexedDB'], conflictResolution: 'latest' }, debug: { enabled: true, verbosity: 'normal' }, }); debug takes an object. StrataConfig has no onLog callback. Compression currently supports the bundled 'lz' algorithm.

const isDevelopment = import.meta.env.DEV; const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: isDevelopment ? 'app-dev' : 'app', defaultStorages: isDevelopment ? ['memory', 'localStorage'] : ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], debug: { enabled: isDevelopment }, }); Keep encryption passwords outside source code and configuration files. Pass a user-provided password to the operation when encryption is needed: const encryptedStorage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true } }); await encryptedStorage.set('private-draft', draft, { encrypt: true, encryptionPassword: password, });

import { Capacitor } from '@capacitor/core'; import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor'; const native = Capacitor.isNativePlatform(); const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'cross-platform-app', defaultStorages: native ? ['sqlite', 'preferences', 'memory'] : ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], }); if (native) await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage); Native adapters are registered separately. adapters.sqlite accepts filename; its low-level SqliteAdapter constructor accepts database and table for separate stores. adapters.secure and adapters.preferences accept booleans, not biometric, iCloud, or App Group options.
const storage = defineStorage({ compression: enableCompression ? { enabled: true, threshold: 1024 } : undefined, ttl: enableExpiry ? { defaultTTL: 3_600_000 } : undefined, });

const userStorage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'user-data' }); const cacheStorage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'cache', defaultStorages: ['memory', 'localStorage'], ttl: { defaultTTL: 300_000 }, }); Namespaces isolate logical keys. They do not create separate IndexedDB object stores or SQLite tables.
Configuration Guide API Reference Web Platform Guide

Strata can notify another browser tab about a change to a supported shared adapter. A notification helps a view refresh; it does not make two concurrent writes atomic or synchronize an authenticated session.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ sync: { enabled: true, storages: ['localStorage'] }, }); async function applySavedTheme(): Promise<void> { const theme = await storage.get<'light' | 'dark'>('theme', { storage: 'localStorage', }); document.documentElement.dataset.theme = theme ?? 'light'; } const unsubscribe = storage.subscribe(change => { if (change.key === 'theme' && change.source === 'remote') { void applySavedTheme(); } }); await applySavedTheme(); await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'localStorage' }); // Call unsubscribe() when this view is removed. A tab receiving a remote event rereads the value; the event itself is not a durable record. Test two real tabs and a reload in your target browser.

Keep credentials and session validity under your server or identity provider. Do not place an auth token in localStorage or broadcast it through Strata. For an existing server-owned session, you may publish a non-secret hint and recheck the server in other tabs: const stopSessionHints = storage.subscribe(change => { if (change.key === 'session-check' && change.source === 'remote') { void refreshSessionFromServer(); } }); await storage.set('session-check', Date.now(), { storage: 'localStorage', }); // Call stopSessionHints() when this view is removed. The hint does not log a tab in or out. Only the server's response determines session state.

Memory is local to one page or process, so it is not a cross-tab transport. A subscription must be cleaned up when its owner is removed. Multiple tabs changing one value can still race. Use a server-side operation or another coordinated protocol when order and uniqueness matter. StorageOptions has no per-call syncEnabled switch. Configure sync on the instance and choose adapters deliberately. See the sync reference for the configuration surface.

Strata Storage can hold pending writes. It doesn't supply a server, conflict policy or delivery guarantee. Your backend must validate the request, authorize the user and treat a repeated operation ID as the same write. Queue and replay Recovery boundaries

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'draft-sync' }); type PendingDraft = { id: string; draftId: string; title: string; }; async function queueDraft(draftId: string, title: string): Promise<string> { const id = crypto.randomUUID(); const pending: PendingDraft = { id, draftId, title }; await storage.set(`outbox:${id}`, pending, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); return id; } async function replayDrafts(): Promise<void> { const keys = await storage.keys(/^outbox:/, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); for (const key of keys) { const pending = await storage.get<PendingDraft>(key, { storage: 'indexedDB', }); if (!pending) continue; try { const response = await fetch('/api/drafts', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Idempotency-Key': pending.id, }, body: JSON.stringify({ draftId: pending.draftId, title: pending.title, }), }); if (!response.ok) continue; await storage.remove(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); } catch { // Keep this write for the next retry. } } } /api/drafts stands for your own authenticated endpoint. It must deduplicate Idempotency-Key and return 2xx only after it has accepted the write; a 4xx/5xx response leaves the local record queued. Call replayDrafts() on startup, resume and a possible reconnection. An online event is a hint, not proof that the request will succeed.

Each operation has its own storage key, so replay doesn't replace a whole queue and erase writes added during the loop. Two tabs can still replay the same key, and a crash can happen after server success but before local removal. Server idempotency handles both cases. For concurrent edits of the same draft, define a revision and conflict policy on the server; this example does not resolve them. query() matches decoded value fields, not physical key names or value.* paths. Use keys(/^outbox:/, { storage: 'indexedDB' }) to find the outbox, and keep account tokens in your server-owned session rather than this client store.

Strata uses Web Crypto for encrypted values. Create an instance with encryption enabled, then provide a password at the operation or instance level. A plain defineStorage() instance does not initialize the encryption manager, even if a later set() passes encrypt: true.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true } }); const password = await askUserForPassword(); await storage.set('private-draft', { text: 'A draft' }, { encryptionPassword: password, }); const draft = await storage.get<{ text: string }>('private-draft', { encryptionPassword: password, }); The password must be available again to decrypt the value. Do not hard-code it or save it beside the encrypted data.

const storage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true, password }, }); await storage.set('private-draft', { text: 'A draft' }); const draft = await storage.get('private-draft'); The configured password applies to encrypted operations on that instance. Protect it in the calling application.

const storage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true } }); await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { encrypt: false }); await storage.set('private-draft', draft, { encrypt: true, encryptionPassword: password, }); const savedTheme = await storage.get('theme'); const savedDraft = await storage.get('private-draft', { encryptionPassword: password, }); When encryption is enabled globally, mark each intentionally plain write with encrypt: false.

Use an application-owned unlock step. Do not treat a missing verification value as a successful unlock. For example, create a marker after the user first sets a password, then require that marker on later unlocks: const storage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true } }); async function createPassword(password: string): Promise<void> { await storage.set('_verification', 'ready', { encryptionPassword: password }); } async function unlock(password: string): Promise<boolean> { try { return await storage.get<string>('_verification', { encryptionPassword: password, }) === 'ready'; } catch { return false; } } This checks whether the supplied password decrypts the marker. It is a local example, not an account authentication system.

Strata derives an encryption key from the supplied password with PBKDF2. The encryption config accepts iterations, saltLength, keyLength, and algorithm. It generates a fresh salt for each encrypted write, so the application does not need to hash the password itself. const storage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true, iterations: 600_000, saltLength: 16, keyLength: 256, algorithm: 'AES-GCM', }, });

A File is not stored as a live browser object. Convert its bytes to a serializable value before writing, and size it for the chosen adapter's quota: const bytes = new Uint8Array(await file.arrayBuffer()); await storage.set(`file:${file.name}`, Array.from(bytes), { storage: 'indexedDB', encrypt: true, encryptionPassword: password, });

async function saveDraft(formId: string, value: unknown, password: string) { await storage.set(`form:${formId}`, value, { encrypt: true, encryptionPassword: password, ttl: 3_600_000, }); } Keep the password available for a later read, and remove the draft when the user discards it.
Encryption Guide Encryption API

get() returns null when a key is absent. A storage operation can still reject because the adapter is unavailable, the value is invalid, quota is exhausted or an encrypted value cannot be read. Catch the operation where your UI can show a retry or recovery path. Handle a failed write Try persistent adapters in order Encryption failures

import { defineStorage, QuotaExceededError, ValidationError, } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); async function saveDraft(title: string): Promise<'saved' | 'retry'> { try { await storage.set('draft', { title }, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); return 'saved'; } catch (error) { if (error instanceof QuotaExceededError) { // Offer a way to free space or export the draft. return 'retry'; } if (error instanceof ValidationError) { // Fix the invalid key or value at the call site. throw error; } throw error; } } A null read isn't a write error, and a failed write shouldn't be presented as saved. Store a draft in memory only if losing it on reload is acceptable.

The storage option can list adapters by availability, but a write failure after selection is not a promise to retry the next backend. To handle write failures, attempt each adapter yourself: import type { StorageType } from 'strata-storage'; async function saveWithFallback(value: string): Promise<StorageType> { const choices: StorageType[] = ['indexedDB', 'localStorage']; for (const adapter of choices) { try { await storage.set('draft', value, { storage: adapter }); return adapter; } catch { // Try the next persistent adapter. } } throw new Error('The draft could not be saved in this browser.'); } Record the returned adapter if later reads must target the same place. A browser may deny both paths.

An encrypted read needs the same user-supplied password used for the write. Configure encryption on the instance before using encrypt: true; see the encryption guide. EncryptionError lets you offer a password retry without treating the value as absent. There is no StrataConfig.onError callback and no NotFoundError for a missing key. Attach error reporting in your own catch block, and avoid logging the value or password.

Copy-pasteable examples for syncing Strata Storage through Firebase (Cloud Firestore or the Realtime Database). See the Firebase guide for the full configuration reference. Install the optional peer dependency with yarn add firebase.

import { Strata, defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { enableFirebaseSync } from 'strata-storage/firebase'; const storage = defineStorage(); await enableFirebaseSync(storage, { apiKey: 'YOUR_API_KEY', authDomain: 'your-app.firebaseapp.com', projectId: 'your-app', appId: 'YOUR_APP_ID', firestore: true, }); // Write/read against Firestore await storage.set('profile', { name: 'Ada', theme: 'dark' }, { storage: 'firestore' }); const profile = await storage.get('profile', { storage: 'firestore' }); // React to remote changes from other devices/users const unsubscribe = storage.subscribe( (change) => { if (change.source === 'remote') { console.log('Remote update:', change.key, change.newValue); } }, { storage: 'firestore' }, ); // later: unsubscribe();

import { Strata, defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { enableFirebaseSync } from 'strata-storage/firebase'; const storage = defineStorage(); await enableFirebaseSync(storage, { apiKey: 'YOUR_API_KEY', authDomain: 'your-app.firebaseapp.com', projectId: 'your-app', appId: 'YOUR_APP_ID', realtimeDatabase: true, }); await storage.set('counter', 0, { storage: 'realtime' }); storage.subscribe( (change) => console.log('counter is now', change.newValue), { storage: 'realtime' }, );

The Firebase adapters store values as-is unless encryption is enabled on the Strata instance. Configure encryption before the first write, then pass a password for each encrypted operation: const encryptedStorage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true } }); await enableFirebaseSync(encryptedStorage, { apiKey: 'YOUR_API_KEY', authDomain: 'your-app.firebaseapp.com', projectId: 'your-app', appId: 'YOUR_APP_ID', firestore: true, }); await encryptedStorage.set('secret', sensitiveValue, { storage: 'firestore', encrypt: true, encryptionPassword: userProvidedPassword, });

A local draft can restore small text fields after a reload. It doesn't submit the form or save files on a server. Keep passwords, payment details and other sensitive fields out of browser draft storage. Draft operations Schedule a save Recovery boundary

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'profile-form' }); const draftOptions = { storage: 'localStorage' as const }; type Fields = { displayName: string; bio: string }; type Draft = { fields: Fields; updatedAt: number }; async function saveDraft(fields: Fields): Promise<void> { await storage.set('draft', { fields, updatedAt: Date.now(), } satisfies Draft, draftOptions); } async function loadDraft(): Promise<Draft | null> { return storage.get<Draft>('draft', draftOptions); } async function discardDraft(): Promise<void> { await storage.remove('draft', draftOptions); } Call loadDraft() before filling the form fields. null means there is no saved draft. Await saveDraft() before telling the user that the draft is saved.

let saveTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined; let writes: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve(); function scheduleDraftSave( fields: Fields, onFailure: (error: unknown) => void, ): void { clearTimeout(saveTimer); const snapshot = { ...fields }; saveTimer = setTimeout(() => { writes = writes.then(() => saveDraft(snapshot)).catch(onFailure); }, 500); } function stopDraftAutoSave(): void { clearTimeout(saveTimer); } Call scheduleDraftSave() after a field changes and stopDraftAutoSave() when the form view closes. The queued Promise serializes writes so an older save doesn't finish after a newer one. A write can still fail; keep the form visible and show a retry instead of claiming success.

localStorage quota and availability vary by browser. Test restore after reload and after a failed write. Form submission is confirmed by your server, and a file upload needs its own server-issued upload ID and retry protocol; a stored progress percentage cannot resume bytes by itself.
Using Strata Storage with Angular applications.
yarn add strata-storage @angular/core and @angular/forms are optional peer dependencies (>= 21.0.6).

For standalone Angular apps, provideStrata() registers StrataService for injection. Pass a pre-created instance (provider-free pattern) or a config object — both are supported. The instance is held in the STRATA_INSTANCE injection token. // main.ts import { bootstrapApplication } from '@angular/platform-browser'; import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { provideStrata } from 'strata-storage/angular'; import { AppComponent } from './app/app.component'; const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage'] }); bootstrapApplication(AppComponent, { providers: [ provideStrata(storage), // or, to let it build the instance from config: // provideStrata({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage'] }), ], }); StrataService exposes the storage operations as RxJS Observables, gated on initialization: import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core'; import { StrataService } from 'strata-storage/angular'; @Component({ selector: 'app-user-profile', standalone: true, template: `
{{ user.name }}
`, }) export class UserProfileComponent implements OnInit { user: any; constructor(private storage: StrataService) {} ngOnInit() { // get() returns Observable this.storage.get('current-user').subscribe((u) => (this.user = u)); } updateUser(data: any) { this.storage.set('current-user', data).subscribe(() => (this.user = data)); } } watch(key) emits the current value and re-emits on changes; ready$ resolves once the instance is initialized.

The NgModule path still works. StrataModule.forRoot(config) builds an instance from config and provides StrataService, the storage/ttl pipes, and the [strataStorage] directive. import { NgModule } from '@angular/core'; import { StrataModule } from 'strata-storage/angular'; @NgModule({ imports: [ StrataModule.forRoot({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage'], }), ], }) export class AppModule {}

import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core'; import { StrataService } from 'strata-storage/angular'; @Component({ selector: 'app-user-profile', template: `

{{ user.name }}

{{ user.email }}

` }) export class UserProfileComponent implements OnInit { user: any; constructor(private storage: StrataService) {} async ngOnInit() { this.user = await this.storage.get('current-user'); } async updateUser(data: any) { await this.storage.set('current-user', data); this.user = data; } }

Pick one wiring style: provider-free createStrataHooks(instance) (recommended, 2.5.0+) or wrap your tree in <StrataProvider> — you don't need both. Handle Loading States: hooks return null until the first read resolves — guard on loading and null-check before use. Error Boundaries: Wrap storage operations in error boundaries Type Safety: Use TypeScript for better type inference Cleanup: Provider-bound hooks unsubscribe automatically; clean up any manual subscribe() calls in useEffect cleanup

yarn add strata-storage vue is an optional peer dependency (>= 3.5.26).

No plugin install required. Create one instance with defineStorage() and bind the composables to it with createStrataComposables(), then use them in any component's setup(). // storage.ts import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { createStrataComposables } from 'strata-storage/vue'; export const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage'] }); export const { useStorage, useStorageQuery, useStorageTTL, useStorageSize } = createStrataComposables(storage); <script setup lang="ts"> import { useStorage } from './storage'; // value is a reactive Ref<T | null> const { value: theme, update, loading } = useStorage<string>('theme', 'light'); </script> <template> <button v-if="!loading" @click="update(theme === 'light' ? 'dark' : 'light')"> Theme: {{ theme }} </button> </template> useStorage(key, defaultValue?, options?) returns { value, loading, error, refresh, update, remove } — value is a reactive Ref, update(next) writes (or removes when next is null). The built-in composables (useStorage, useStorageQuery, useStorageTTL, useStorageSize) also accept an optional Strata instance as a trailing argument if you prefer not to pre-bind them. You can also use the instance directly — it works immediately, no setup call: import { storage } from './storage'; await storage.set('lastSeen', Date.now());

The StrataPlugin still works for apps that prefer dependency injection. Install it once; the composables then resolve the instance from Vue's provide/inject. import { createApp } from 'vue'; import { StrataPlugin } from 'strata-storage/vue'; import App from './App.vue'; createApp(App) .use(StrataPlugin, { defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage'] }) .mount('#app'); <script setup lang="ts"> import { useStorage } from 'strata-storage/vue'; const { value: username, update } = useStorage<string>('username', 'Guest'); </script>
useStorage returns { value, update, ... } (not a bare ref). Wrap it in a computed getter/setter to drive v-model.
Store a whole settings object under one key and mirror it into a local reactive for v-model.

// main.js import { createApp } from 'vue'; import { StrataPlugin } from 'strata-storage/vue'; const app = createApp(App); app.use(StrataPlugin, { namespace: 'my-app', defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage'] }); app.mount('#app');

Persist a draft with the built-in useStorage composable: mirror the stored object into a local reactive and write it back on every edit. (For a reusable wrapper, see the useFormPersistence composable in the Vue Composables example.)

Prepare one storage instance after the Ionic platform is ready. defineStorage() registers the web adapters, and registerCapacitorAdapters() adds native adapters when the app runs through Capacitor. import { Injectable } from '@angular/core'; import { Platform } from '@ionic/angular'; import { Capacitor } from '@capacitor/core'; import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor'; @Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' }) export class StorageService { private readonly storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'ionic-app', defaultStorages: Capacitor.isNativePlatform() ? ['sqlite', 'preferences', 'memory'] : ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], }); private readonly ready: Promise<void>; constructor(platform: Platform) { this.ready = platform.ready().then(() => registerCapacitorAdapters(this.storage)); } async set<T>(key: string, value: T): Promise<void> { await this.ready; await this.storage.set(key, value); } async get<T>(key: string): Promise<T | null> { await this.ready; return this.storage.get<T>(key); } } A screen can call await storageService.set('draft', draft) and read it with await storageService.get<Draft>('draft'). Test the web path in a browser and the native path in an iOS or Android build. See the Capacitor guide and device verification guide.

Examples of implementing data migrations in Strata Storage. Migrations are an experimental, adapter-level utility (MigrationManager). They are not configured through StrataConfig; you run them explicitly against an initialized storage adapter. See the Migration API and Migrations Guide.

import { MigrationManager, LocalStorageAdapter } from 'strata-storage'; import type { Migration } from 'strata-storage'; const adapter = new LocalStorageAdapter(); await adapter.initialize(); const migrations: Migration[] = [ { version: 1, up: async (a) => { const keys = await a.keys(); const now = Date.now(); for (const key of keys) { const record = await a.get<Record<string, unknown>>(key); if (record && record.value && !('created' in record.value)) { await a.set(key, { value: { ...record.value, created: now }, created: record.created, updated: now, }); } } }, }, ]; const manager = new MigrationManager(); migrations.forEach((m) => manager.register(m)); await manager.migrate(adapter, 1);

const migration: Migration = { version: 2, up: async (a) => { const keys = await a.keys(/^user:/); for (const key of keys) { const record = await a.get<{ name: string; avatar?: string; email: string; phone?: string; settings?: unknown; }>(key); if (!record) continue; const old = record.value; await a.set(key, { value: { profile: { name: old.name, avatar: old.avatar }, contact: { email: old.email, phone: old.phone }, settings: old.settings ?? {}, }, created: record.created, updated: Date.now(), }); } }, down: async (a) => { const keys = await a.keys(/^user:/); for (const key of keys) { const record = await a.get<{ profile?: { name?: string; avatar?: string }; contact?: { email?: string; phone?: string }; settings?: unknown; }>(key); if (!record) continue; const updated = record.value; await a.set(key, { value: { name: updated.profile?.name, avatar: updated.profile?.avatar, email: updated.contact?.email, phone: updated.contact?.phone, settings: updated.settings, }, created: record.created, updated: Date.now(), }); } }, };

For large data sets, process keys in batches inside the migration to keep memory use bounded: const migrations: Migration[] = [ { version: 1, up: async (a) => { const allKeys = (await a.keys()).filter((k) => k.startsWith('user:')); const batchSize = 100; for (let offset = 0; offset < allKeys.length; offset += batchSize) { const batch = allKeys.slice(offset, offset + batchSize); for (const key of batch) { const record = await a.get<Record<string, unknown>>(key); if (!record) continue; await a.set(key, { value: { ...record.value, roles: ['user'] }, created: record.created, updated: Date.now(), }); } console.log(`Migrated ${Math.min(offset + batchSize, allKeys.length)} items`); } }, }, ];

function isCorrupted(data: unknown): boolean { return !data || typeof data !== 'object' || !('id' in (data as object)); } function fixData(data: Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown> { return { ...data, id: data.id ?? generateId(), repaired: true, repairedAt: Date.now(), }; } const migrations: Migration[] = [ { version: 3, up: async (a) => { const keys = await a.keys(); for (const key of keys) { const record = await a.get<Record<string, unknown>>(key); if (record && isCorrupted(record.value)) { await a.set(key, { value: fixData(record.value), created: record.created, updated: Date.now(), }); console.log(`Fixed corrupted data: ${key}`); } } }, }, ];

Each migration receives a single adapter, so moving data between two backends is done directly — read from the source adapter, write to the destination: import { LocalStorageAdapter, IndexedDBAdapter } from 'strata-storage'; const source = new LocalStorageAdapter(); const target = new IndexedDBAdapter(); await source.initialize(); await target.initialize(); const keys = await source.keys(); console.log(`Migrating ${keys.length} items to IndexedDB`); for (const key of keys) { const record = await source.get(key); if (record !== null) { await target.set(key, record); await source.remove(key); } }

const formatMigrations: Migration[] = [ { version: 5, up: async (a) => { const keys = await a.keys(); for (const key of keys) { const record = await a.get<{ created?: unknown; updated?: unknown }>(key); if (!record) continue; const value = { ...record.value }; let changed = false; if (typeof value.created === 'number') { value.created = new Date(value.created).toISOString(); changed = true; } if (typeof value.updated === 'number') { value.updated = new Date(value.updated).toISOString(); changed = true; } if (changed) { await a.set(key, { value, created: record.created, updated: Date.now() }); } } }, }, ];

Snapshot the adapter's data before migrating, and restore it if the migration fails: import { MigrationManager, StorageAdapter } from 'strata-storage'; async function runSafely( manager: MigrationManager, adapter: StorageAdapter, targetVersion: number, ) { // 1. Back up current data const keys = await adapter.keys(); const backup: Array<[string, unknown]> = []; for (const key of keys) backup.push([key, await adapter.get(key)]); try { // 2. Run the migration await manager.migrate(adapter, targetVersion); } catch (error) { console.error('Migration failed, restoring backup:', error); // 3. Restore from backup for (const [key, record] of backup) { if (record !== null) await adapter.set(key, record as never); } throw error; } }

A Strata instance can select from its registered adapters. The default list chooses the first available adapter at initialization; a later write error is not automatically retried elsewhere.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'sessionStorage', 'memory'], }); await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First pass' }); Use an explicit array in an operation when the caller needs its own availability preference: await storage.set('draft', draft, { storage: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage'], });

await storage.set('profile', profile, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); await storage.set('tab', 'details', { storage: 'sessionStorage' }); await storage.set('temporary-filter', filter, { storage: 'memory', ttl: 300_000 }); Choose an adapter for the value's lifetime and quota. memory is lost when the page ends; sessionStorage is tab scoped.

import { Capacitor } from '@capacitor/core'; import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor'; const native = Capacitor.isNativePlatform(); const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: native ? ['sqlite', 'preferences', 'memory'] : ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], }); if (native) await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage); Native stores need adapter registration and device verification. secure is not a browser fallback.

const keys = await storage.keys(/^draft:/, { storage: 'localStorage' }); for (const key of keys) { const value = await storage.get(key, { storage: 'localStorage' }); if (value === null) continue; await storage.set(key, value, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); const copied = await storage.get(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); if (copied !== null) await storage.remove(key, { storage: 'localStorage' }); } Test migrations against real data before removing the old key. A non-null read alone does not prove object equality; add application-specific verification when that matters.
Strata does not move values between adapters according to their current usage. Select the adapter explicitly using your application's quota and retention rules.
For cross-tab notifications, configure sync and subscribe to changes. It is not an atomic merge of simultaneous writes. See the cross-tab sync guide.

function storageForKey(key: string): 'indexedDB' | 'memory' { return key.startsWith('draft:') ? 'indexedDB' : 'memory'; } await storage.set(key, value, { storage: storageForKey(key) }); Do not route a browser value to a native adapter that has not been registered, or treat local storage as the server's authentication authority.

Strata can keep a local draft while the network is unavailable. Sending that draft to a server is an application protocol: the server must accept an idempotency key and return a successful HTTP status before the client removes its queued write.

This browser example keeps each queued write under its own IndexedDB key. Adding a new write during a replay does not overwrite the current queue. Replace /api/notes with your own endpoint, and make the server treat repeated Idempotency-Key values as the same operation. import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); type PendingNote = { id: string; title: string; }; async function queueNote(title: string): Promise<string> { const id = crypto.randomUUID(); await storage.set(`outbox:${id}`, { id, title } satisfies PendingNote, { storage: 'indexedDB', }); return id; } async function replayNotes(): Promise<void> { const keys = await storage.keys(/^outbox:/, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); for (const key of keys) { const note = await storage.get<PendingNote>(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); if (!note) continue; try { const response = await fetch('/api/notes', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Idempotency-Key': note.id, }, body: JSON.stringify({ title: note.title }), }); if (!response.ok) continue; await storage.remove(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); } catch { // Keep the write for a later retry after a network error. } } } window.addEventListener('online', () => { void replayNotes(); }); Call replayNotes() on app startup and on resume too. The online event only signals a possible connection; a request can still fail. A server that does not deduplicate Idempotency-Key can create duplicate notes after a retry, so do not use this pattern without that server contract. Multi-tab writers also need coordination if the same queued key can replay in two tabs at once.

A service worker can cache HTTP responses through the browser Cache API. Strata's Cache adapter requires window and does not run in a service worker. // In a service worker, for same-origin GET requests you choose to cache. self.addEventListener('fetch', event => { if (event.request.method !== 'GET' || new URL(event.request.url).origin !== self.location.origin) return; event.respondWith((async () => { const cache = await caches.open('app-responses-v1'); const cached = await cache.match(event.request); if (cached) return cached; const response = await fetch(event.request); if (response.ok) await cache.put(event.request, response.clone()); return response; })()); }); Choose cacheable routes deliberately. A cached response can be stale, and this example has no eviction policy. For Strata data, use an adapter appropriate to the browser page and test the read path after reload.

Storage speed depends on the adapter, browser or device, value size and the rest of your application. Measure the round-trip you actually use. The Strata API has no setMany() method and no indexedDB.indexes configuration. Measure a bounded sample Choose the storage path Query costs

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); const samples = Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, index) => ({ id: index, title: `Draft ${index}`, })); const started = performance.now(); for (const item of samples) { await storage.set(`draft:${item.id}`, item, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); } const writeMilliseconds = performance.now() - started; const readStarted = performance.now(); const first = await storage.get<{ id: number; title: string }>( 'draft:0', { storage: 'indexedDB' }, ); const readMilliseconds = performance.now() - readStarted; Run this in each target browser with representative values. writeMilliseconds and readMilliseconds are measurements from that run, not a package-wide speed claim. Clean up the sample keys when the measurement ends.

memory loses values on reload. localStorage writes synchronously in the browser. indexedDB is an async browser backend. Set the adapter explicitly when your data's persistence matters: await storage.set('preview', { open: true }, { storage: 'memory' }); await storage.set('draft', { title: 'Working copy' }, { storage: 'indexedDB', }); Compression is optional. It only runs when the instance is configured for it, and it may keep a value uncompressed if the output would not be smaller: const compressedStorage = defineStorage({ compression: { enabled: true, threshold: 1024 }, }); const articleText = 'A representative paragraph. '.repeat(100); await compressedStorage.set('article', articleText, { storage: 'indexedDB', compress: true, }); Replace the sample articleText with your application's value. Compare a representative write and read with compression on and off before enabling it for a workload.

storage.query() scans selected adapter keys and decodes each value before matching. Strata doesn't expose IndexedDB indexes or SQL indexes through its key/value API. Use a server-side query for large or shared datasets; keep local queries bounded and measure them on the target device.

Strata Storage's query() reads values from the selected adapter and matches fields on the decoded value. It doesn't query storage keys, wrapper metadata or database indexes. A browser round-trip Operators and result options Limits

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); await storage.set('member:1', { name: 'Sam', status: 'active', age: 27, tags: ['team'], }, { storage: 'memory' }); await storage.set('member:2', { name: 'Lee', status: 'paused', age: 19, tags: ['trial'], }, { storage: 'memory' }); const active = await storage.query<{ name: string; status: string; age: number; tags: string[]; }>({ status: 'active' }, { storage: 'memory' }); // active contains { key: 'member:1', value: { ... } } The object passed to query() names value fields directly. Use status, not value.status; the returned key is outside the value and isn't a condition field.

const adultsInTeam = await storage.query<{ name: string; status: string; age: number; tags: string[]; }>({ age: { $gte: 18 }, tags: { $in: ['team'] }, }, { storage: 'memory', sort: { age: -1 }, skip: 0, limit: 10, }); Supported comparisons include $eq, $ne, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in, $nin, $regex, $exists and $type. $and, $or and $not combine conditions. $in matches an array field when any listed operand appears in that array; it doesn't inspect Strata's wrapper tags. sort, skip and limit shape the returned array after matching. select projects value fields. The result remains an array of { key, value } records.

query() scans selected adapter keys and decodes their values. The indexedDB and sqlite adapters don't expose database indexes through StrataConfig. For large or shared datasets, query and aggregate on your server; this client-side API is for bounded local data.

The server owns authentication. The hook can display its session state, but a value in Strata Storage is not proof of sign-in. This example assumes the host app exposes a cookie-backed /api/session endpoint: function useAuth() { const [account, setAccount] = useState(null); const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true); useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/session', { credentials: 'include' }) .then(response => response.ok ? response.json() : null) .then(setAccount) .finally(() => setLoading(false)); }, []); return { account, loading }; } Keep the browser session credential in a server-issued HttpOnly cookie. Strata's JavaScript cookie adapter cannot create one.

function useOfflineQueue() { const storage = useStrata(); const [queue, setQueue] = useState([]); const [online, setOnline] = useState(navigator.onLine); useEffect(() => { // Load queue storage.get('offline_queue').then(data => { if (data) setQueue(data); }); // Monitor online status const handleOnline = () => { setOnline(true); processQueue(); }; const handleOffline = () => setOnline(false); window.addEventListener('online', handleOnline); window.addEventListener('offline', handleOffline); return () => { window.removeEventListener('online', handleOnline); window.removeEventListener('offline', handleOffline); }; }, []); const addToQueue = async (action) => { const updated = [...queue, { ...action, id: Date.now() }]; await storage.set('offline_queue', updated); setQueue(updated); if (online) processQueue(); }; const processQueue = async () => { const pending = await storage.get('offline_queue') || []; for (const action of pending) { try { await processAction(action); // Remove from queue const remaining = pending.filter(a => a.id !== action.id); await storage.set('offline_queue', remaining); setQueue(remaining); } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to process:', action); break; // Stop on first failure } } }; return { addToQueue, queue, online }; }

function usePersistentState(key, initialValue, options = {}) { const storage = useStrata(); const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue); const [loaded, setLoaded] = useState(false); // Load initial value useEffect(() => { storage.get(key).then(value => { if (value !== null) setState(value); setLoaded(true); }); }, [key]); // Update storage when state changes useEffect(() => { if (loaded) { storage.set(key, state, options); } }, [state, loaded]); return [state, setState, loaded]; }

Create the instance with encryption enabled before wrapping it in a hook. Passing encrypt: true to an unconfigured useStrata() instance does not initialise the encryption manager. import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const encryptedStorage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true } }); function useEncryptedStorage(password: string) { return useMemo(() => ({ set: (key: string, value: unknown) => encryptedStorage.set(key, value, { encrypt: true, encryptionPassword: password, }), get: (key: string) => encryptedStorage.get(key, { encryptionPassword: password, }), remove: (key: string) => encryptedStorage.remove(key), }), [password]); }

Strata Storage 3.1.4 does not register React Native storage adapters. The native adapters exported from strata-storage/capacitor use Capacitor plugins and require a Capacitor runtime. A React Native app cannot use them by selecting secure, sqlite or preferences in defaultStorages. For a web or Capacitor app, use the Capacitor example and platform guide. For React Native, use a storage library with adapters built for that runtime. No React Native integration or biometric option is claimed by this package.

A cart in localStorage can survive a browser reload. It is a draft of the shopper's intent, not an order record: prices, stock, discounts and tax must be checked by the server before checkout. Save and read a cart Limits

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'shop-cart' }); const cartOptions = { storage: 'localStorage' as const }; type CartItem = { productId: string; name: string; quantity: number }; type Cart = { items: CartItem[] }; async function readCart(): Promise<Cart> { return (await storage.get<Cart>('cart', cartOptions)) ?? { items: [] }; } async function addItem(productId: string, name: string, quantity = 1): Promise<void> { if (!Number.isInteger(quantity) || quantity < 1) { throw new Error('Quantity must be a positive whole number.'); } const cart = await readCart(); const item = cart.items.find(entry => entry.productId === productId); if (item) item.quantity += quantity; else cart.items.push({ productId, name, quantity }); await storage.set('cart', cart, cartOptions); } async function removeItem(productId: string): Promise<void> { const cart = await readCart(); cart.items = cart.items.filter(item => item.productId !== productId); await storage.set('cart', cart, cartOptions); } async function clearCart(): Promise<void> { await storage.remove('cart', cartOptions); } readCart() returns an empty cart when the key is absent. Surface write failures to the shopper before saying an item was saved.

A cart update is a read followed by a write, not an atomic transaction. Two tabs can race and overwrite each other's changes. If a shopper signs in or checks out, merge and validate the cart on your server with a conflict policy; don't treat localStorage as shared account state. query() matches fields inside stored values. It cannot filter physical keys or wrapper fields such as key and value.timestamp. If you collect cart events, record the event name and timestamp in each value, then aggregate reports on the server after consent.

A TTL gives a stored value an expiry time. Strata returns null after that time and can clean expired records from adapters. Expiry is a local cache rule, not a server session or authorization boundary. Relative and absolute expiry Sliding expiry Inspect and change expiry

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); const options = { storage: 'memory' as const }; await storage.set('preview', { title: 'Working copy' }, { ...options, ttl: 5 * 60 * 1000, }); await storage.set('event-data', { count: 3 }, { ...options, expireAt: Date.now() + 60 * 60 * 1000, }); const preview = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('preview', options); // After its expiry, preview is null. ttl is a duration in milliseconds from the write. expireAt is a future Date or epoch-millisecond timestamp. A past expireAt doesn't create a future expiry; use a relative expression when the example should keep working next year.

const slidingStorage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['memory'], ttl: { defaultTTL: 30 * 60 * 1000, slidingTTL: true, }, }); await slidingStorage.set('draft', 'In progress', { storage: 'memory', }); const draft = await slidingStorage.get<string>('draft', { storage: 'memory', }); With slidingTTL and a configured defaultTTL, each successful read of an unexpired value refreshes its expiry. A per-write sliding: true flag alone does not supply the duration needed for a later read to extend it.

const remainingMs = await storage.getTTL('preview', options); const soon = await storage.getExpiring(10 * 60 * 1000, options); for (const item of soon) { const key = item.key; const expiresInMs = item.expiresIn; // Use key and expiresInMs in your UI. } await storage.extendTTL('preview', 5 * 60 * 1000, options); await storage.persist('preview', options); getTTL() returns null for a key without expiry or one that is absent. getExpiring() returns { key, expiresIn }, not { key, ttl }. extendTTL() adds time to the current expiry; persist() removes expiry, but a memory value still disappears on reload. Run cleanupExpired(options) when you need to remove expired records immediately instead of waiting for a read or scheduled cleanup. See the TTL guide for configuration and adapter behavior.

Strata Storage holds client-side key-value data. It does not authenticate a user, issue a session, or enforce server authorization. The host application must do those jobs. For a browser app, keep the session credential in a server-issued HttpOnly cookie; JavaScript and Strata's cookie adapter cannot create one.

The following endpoints belong to the example host application, not to Strata Storage. The server validates credentials, sets or clears its session cookie, and returns only non-secret account data to the browser. import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const uiStorage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'account-ui', defaultStorages: ['sessionStorage', 'memory'], }); async function signIn(email: string, password: string) { const response = await fetch('/api/session', { method: 'POST', credentials: 'include', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }), }); if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Sign-in failed'); const account = await response.json(); await uiStorage.set('lastAccountView', account.defaultView, { storage: 'sessionStorage', }); return account; } async function signOut() { const response = await fetch('/api/session', { method: 'DELETE', credentials: 'include', }); if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Sign-out failed'); await uiStorage.clear({ storage: 'sessionStorage' }); } The UI preference is a convenience value, not proof that a person is signed in. Read the server session on boot and enforce access on every protected server route.

async function loadAccount() { const response = await fetch('/api/session', { credentials: 'include', }); if (response.status === 401) return null; if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Could not load the session'); return response.json(); } If the application uses Capacitor native storage for a local credential, register the native adapters first and verify the secure read path on device. The secure adapter is not a server authentication system and does not expose a biometric requirement through StorageOptions.

Make the server the authority for sign-in, sign-out, roles and account deletion. Do not store an access or refresh token in localStorage, sessionStorage, or a JavaScript-written cookie merely because the value can be encrypted. Treat Strata values as untrusted input when sending them to a server. Clear temporary account UI data after the server confirms sign-out. Test expiry and recovery with the host application's real session API.
Session state patterns Secure adapter Encryption guide

A Vue composable can wrap one Strata instance for small browser state. This example selects localStorage, enables cross-tab sync, restores the value on mount and unsubscribes on unmount. It isn't a server session or a multi-user database. Composable Usage and limits

import { onMounted, onUnmounted, ref, shallowRef } from 'vue'; import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'vue-example', defaultStorages: ['localStorage'], sync: { enabled: true }, }); const options = { storage: 'localStorage' as const }; export function useStoredValue<T>(key: string, initial: T) { const value = shallowRef<T>(initial); const ready = ref(false); const error = shallowRef<unknown>(null); let active = true; let unsubscribe: (() => void) | undefined; onMounted(async () => { unsubscribe = storage.subscribe(change => { if (change.key !== key || change.source !== 'remote') return; void storage.get<T>(key, options).then(current => { if (active) value.value = current ?? initial; }).catch(cause => { if (active) error.value = cause; }); }, options); try { const stored = await storage.get<T>(key, options); if (active && stored !== null) value.value = stored; } catch (cause) { if (active) error.value = cause; } finally { if (active) ready.value = true; } }); onUnmounted(() => { active = false; unsubscribe?.(); }); async function save(next: T): Promise<void> { try { await storage.set(key, next, options); if (active) value.value = next; } catch (cause) { error.value = cause; throw cause; } } return { value, ready, error, save }; }

Call useStoredValue('draft-title', '') from a component's setup() and replace the returned value through save(). shallowRef tracks replacement, not deep mutations of an object. Show a pending state until ready is true and a retry when error is set. A subscription alone does not enable cross-tab sync; the instance above configures sync.enabled. The localStorage adapter emits local and remote changes. If you select another adapter, use the public StorageType type for its name and verify whether that adapter observes changes. The indexedDB adapter currently reports observable: false, so this subscription pattern must not be copied onto it unchanged.
These examples use Strata Storage for client-side key-value state. The server still owns authentication, payments and shared records.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'my-web-app', defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], }); await storage.set('draft:123', { title: 'First pass' }, { storage: 'indexedDB', }); const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft:123', { storage: 'indexedDB', }); Keep access decisions on the server. A locally stored value does not prove the user is signed in.

The current Strata Cache adapter requires a browser window, so it is not available inside a service worker. Use the browser Cache API directly in the worker for request/response caching, and Strata in the page for application data. // In the page, not the service worker: const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'pwa-drafts' }); await storage.set('draft', draft, { storage: 'indexedDB' });

async function loadDraft(id: string) { const cached = await storage.get(`draft:${id}`, { storage: 'indexedDB', }); if (!navigator.onLine) return cached; const response = await fetch(`/api/drafts/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`); if (!response.ok) return cached; const current = await response.json(); await storage.set(`draft:${id}`, current, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); return current; } This is a cached read. Offline writes need an application-owned outbox, stable operation IDs and server idempotency; caching a draft alone does not sync it later.

const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'site-preferences' }); await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'localStorage' }); Pages on the same origin can read the preference through the same namespace. The strata: physical prefix is applied by default to shared web storage areas.

A cart draft can live locally until the shopper signs in or checks out: const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'cart-draft' }); await storage.set('items', cartItems, { storage: 'localStorage' }); The server must recalculate price, inventory, discounts and payment state. Never take a local cart total as the amount to charge.

const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'dashboard-ui', sync: { enabled: true, storages: ['localStorage'] }, }); await storage.set('layout', layout, { storage: 'localStorage' }); sync is an instance configuration, not an option on an individual set() call. The server remains the source of truth for dashboard data shared among users.

Use Strata for data, not executable JavaScript. Load modules through the browser's normal import path and cache only serializable results when that is useful: const module = await import('./report-view.js'); const result = module.calculate(reportInput); await storage.set('report-summary', result, { storage: 'indexedDB', ttl: 300_000, });
