documents.t: Sync Strata Storage across devices and users with Firebase — either Cloud Firestore or the Realtime Database. Firebase is an optional peer dependency: it is loaded dynamically only when you call enableFirebaseSync, so it adds nothing to your bundle unless you use it. The core package keeps its zero-runtime-dependency guarantee.

# the package itself yarn add strata-storage # Firebase is an OPTIONAL peer dependency — install it only if you use this feature yarn add firebase Import the Firebase helpers from the dedicated entry point: import { enableFirebaseSync, isFirebaseAvailable } from 'strata-storage/firebase';

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { enableFirebaseSync } from 'strata-storage/firebase'; const storage = defineStorage(); await enableFirebaseSync(storage, { apiKey: 'YOUR_API_KEY', authDomain: 'your-app.firebaseapp.com', projectId: 'your-app', appId: 'YOUR_APP_ID', firestore: true, // register the Firestore adapter collectionName: 'strata-storage', // optional (this is the default) }); // Use it like any other store — writes go to Firestore, and onSnapshot pushes // remote changes back into your subscribers. await storage.set('profile', { name: 'Ada' }, { storage: 'firestore' }); const profile = await storage.get('profile', { storage: 'firestore' });

await enableFirebaseSync(storage, { apiKey: 'YOUR_API_KEY', authDomain: 'your-app.firebaseapp.com', projectId: 'your-app', appId: 'YOUR_APP_ID', realtimeDatabase: true, // register the Realtime Database adapter }); await storage.set('counter', 1, { storage: 'realtime' }); You can enable both at once (firestore: true, realtimeDatabase: true) — each registers its own adapter (firestore / realtime).

interface FirebaseSyncConfig { apiKey: string; // required — Firebase web API key authDomain: string; // required projectId: string; // required appId: string; // required storageBucket?: string; messagingSenderId?: string; realtimeDatabase?: boolean; // register the Realtime Database adapter firestore?: boolean; // register the Firestore adapter collectionName?: string; // Firestore collection only (default: 'strata-storage'); the RTDB root is always 'strata-storage' syncInterval?: number; } enableFirebaseSync initializes the Firebase app if one is not already initialized, then registers the requested adapter(s) on your Strata instance via registerAdapter. Target them explicitly with { storage: 'firestore' } or { storage: 'realtime' }, or add them to your defaultStorages order.

firestore realtime Persistence ✅ remote ✅ remote Observable (subscribe) ✅ via onSnapshot ✅ via onValue Queryable ✅ ❌ Storage layout one document per key in collectionName strata-storage/<key> size() returns { total: 0, count: 0 } (not computed) rough estimate Remote changes arrive through your subscribe(...) callback with source: 'remote', so you can distinguish them from local writes.

import { isFirebaseAvailable } from 'strata-storage/firebase'; if (await isFirebaseAvailable()) { await enableFirebaseSync(storage, config); } isFirebaseAvailable() resolves true only when the optional firebase dependency can be imported.

These adapters are not encrypted at rest by Strata (encrypted: false). Data is stored in Firebase as-is. If you need confidentiality, combine this with the Encryption feature (encrypt values before they leave the device) and/or rely on Firebase Security Rules for access control. Secure your Firebase project with Auth + Security Rules — Strata does not manage authentication or authorization. firestore.size() is a stub ({ total: 0, count: 0 }); don't rely on it for quota math. Pricing/quotas are governed by Firebase, not Strata — design your read/write patterns accordingly.
Firebase examples Sync feature Encryption guide
Strata Storage's Capacitor plugin provides preferences (UserDefaults), secure (Keychain), sqlite and filesystem adapters on iOS.
yarn add strata-storage yarn cap sync ios

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor'; const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['sqlite', 'preferences', 'memory'], }); await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage); await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'preferences' }); await storage.set('draft:1', { title: 'First draft' }, { storage: 'sqlite' }); await storage.set('session_token', token, { storage: 'secure', ttl: 3_600_000, }); The helper registers native adapters only inside a Capacitor app. Use the prepared storage instance throughout the application.

Adapter Use for Limit preferences Small app settings Not encrypted; no iCloud sync option in StrataConfig secure Sensitive key-value data No biometric prompt or Keychain accessibility option in StorageOptions sqlite Larger structured key-value sets Top-level Strata has no atomic transaction() API filesystem File-backed JSON values Directory is fixed by the native adapter The Capacitor plugin definitions include lower-level Keychain and UserDefaults methods, but the Strata adapter options do not expose App Groups, a biometric requirement, iCloud sync, or a per-call directory. Use a separately verified native integration if your app needs one of those behaviors.

Run the native device matrix on a simulator or device. Check values after force-quitting and relaunching the app, then confirm the native storage path used by each adapter. A browser test cannot prove Keychain, UserDefaults, SQLite or filesystem persistence.
Capacitor guide SQLite adapter Secure adapter
Strata Storage's browser adapters give one key/value API over several browser storage facilities. The adapter you choose still determines persistence, quota and availability.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], }); await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First pass' }); const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft'); defineStorage() registers memory, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies and the Cache adapter. It initializes lazily. With no explicit storage option, Strata tries your defaultStorages in order and uses the first available registered adapter; it does not measure and choose the fastest backend. To select a backend deliberately: await storage.set('setting', 'dark', { storage: 'localStorage' }); await storage.set('temporary', 'editing', { storage: 'memory' }); await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First pass' }, { storage: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage'], }); Web storage availability and quota depend on the browser, storage settings, browsing mode and device. Test each target browser and a reload round-trip. See the adapter map for what each adapter stores.

const sharedStorage = defineStorage({ sync: { enabled: true } }); const unsubscribe = sharedStorage.subscribe(change => { if (change.source === 'remote') { // Refresh the affected view from storage. } }); // Call unsubscribe() when this view is removed. Cross-tab notifications do not make a write atomic across tabs. Use a server or a coordinated protocol for operations that must not be duplicated.

The Strata Cache adapter requires window and is for JSON-serializable key/value data in browser pages. It is not the browser's request/response cache interface inside a service worker. Use the browser Cache API for an app shell or HTTP responses in that scope: // In a service worker self.addEventListener('install', event => { event.waitUntil((async () => { const cache = await caches.open('app-shell-v1'); await cache.add('/index.html'); })()); }); Choose a cache version and update policy for your app. The sample only shows installation and does not provide an offline fallback or an update flow.

if (navigator.storage?.estimate) { const estimate = await navigator.storage.estimate(); // Inspect estimate.usage and estimate.quota for this browser. } navigator.storage.persist() is a browser permission request, not a guarantee that IndexedDB or Cache data survives every user action. Handle write failures and keep a recovery path for data that matters. For an application outbox, see the offline support example. The server must deduplicate replayed operations.

Strata Storage 3.1.4 requires Node 24.13 or later in the toolchain and ships as ESM. The core package has no runtime dependencies. Framework, Firebase and Capacitor integrations are optional sub-path imports with their own peer requirements.
yarn add strata-storage For another package manager, use its normal package-add command. The core browser entry point is strata-storage.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); await storage.set('installation-check', 'ready', { storage: 'memory' }); const result = await storage.get<string>('installation-check', { storage: 'memory', }); console.log(result); // ready defineStorage() registers the standard web adapters and initializes lazily. The memory check works in a browser page without asking for persistent storage. Then run the Quick Start with the adapter your app will use.

The package exports strata-storage/react, strata-storage/vue and strata-storage/angular. Install the corresponding framework peer in your app and follow its integration example. A basic defineStorage() call needs no framework Provider or plugin.
documents.s: Add a framework binding only when needed

documents.t: Install the optional @capacitor/core peer through your app's package manager and sync the native project after installing the package. Register the adapters before selecting a native backend: import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor'; const storage = defineStorage(); await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage); await storage.set('device-setting', 'ready', { storage: 'preferences' }); const result = await storage.get<string>('device-setting', { storage: 'preferences', }); This snippet requires a running Capacitor iOS or Android app. The registration helper returns without adding native adapters in a browser tab. Run the device verification sequence, including a read after app restart. The Secure adapter uses platform storage but does not expose a biometric prompt option; do not add Face ID usage text solely for this package.
documents.s: Add Capacitor adapters only in a Capacitor app

documents.t: Install the firebase peer only if your app uses the Firebase integration. Its setup and authentication remain your app's responsibility. The core package does not provide a hosted account or automatic cross-device synchronization.

Do not put an encryption password in a browser .env file or compiled config: build tools can embed it in public JavaScript. An encrypted write needs an instance with encryption enabled and a password supplied by a user or other appropriate runtime flow. Follow the encryption guide for the exact options and recovery implications. A server secret belongs only on the server.

“No available storage adapters” usually means a manually constructed new Strata() instance has no registered adapters. Use defineStorage() for the standard browser set, or register the adapter explicitly. A native adapter cannot be selected from an ordinary browser page. Check Capacitor registration and the device runtime. If an encrypted write throws for a missing password, supply a password through the application flow; do not disable the failure or bundle a fixed one. See troubleshooting for further error paths.

The main package exports the Strata class, but new Strata() starts with no registered adapters. Use defineStorage() for the standard web set, or register adapters explicitly before calling storage methods. Native adapters live in the strata-storage/capacitor entry point.

import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], }); await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First draft' }); const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft'); The factory registers the web adapters and initializes lazily on the first operation. Calling initialize() yourself is optional. A manual new Strata() setup must call registerWebAdapters(storage) or storage.registerAdapter(...) before use.

import { Capacitor } from '@capacitor/core'; import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor'; const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: Capacitor.isNativePlatform() ? ['sqlite', 'preferences', 'memory'] : ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], }); await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage); await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First draft' }); registerCapacitorAdapters() registers Preferences, SQLite, Secure and Filesystem on a native Capacitor platform, then refreshes the instance. It does nothing to native registration in a browser. Import it from the Capacitor subpath, not the package root.

The web localStorage and sessionStorage adapters now write with the strata: physical key prefix. The library can adopt its own older unprefixed storage envelopes on read. If an external script reads a physical key directly before Strata loads, configure keyPrefix: false and test that reader before upgrading; configuration explains the ownership check.

Build with the current package exports and inspect every custom new Strata() instance for registration. Read a known pre-upgrade key, write a new value, reload and read it back. On iOS and Android, sync the native project and run the device verification guide. Browser tests cannot prove native persistence.
Your first set() needs an available adapter. The exported storage instance registers the standard web adapters and initialises on first use. You don't construct or initialise it.

yarn add strata-storage The package is ESM-only and requires Node 24.13 or later in your toolchain. It has no runtime dependencies. React, Vue, Angular, Firebase and Capacitor integrations are optional sub-path imports with their own peer requirements.

import { storage } from 'strata-storage'; await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First pass' }); const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft'); console.log(draft?.title); // First pass await storage.remove('draft'); console.log(await storage.has('draft')); // false The default preference order is localStorage, indexedDB, sessionStorage, then memory. The instance also registers cookies and cache; keys(), clear() and size() without a storage option span all registered adapters. subscribe() listens to registered adapters that support change events. The URL adapter is exported but must be registered explicitly. See storage selection before calling a broad clear(). get<T>() returns T | null when you supply T; without it the result is unknown | null. The type parameter describes your data to TypeScript. It does not validate stored data at runtime.

Use defineStorage() when you need a different adapter preference or feature set. It registers the standard web adapters and initialises lazily, just like storage. import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; export const appStorage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'], }); await appStorage.set('theme', 'dark'); const theme = await appStorage.get<string>('theme'); defaultStorages sets preference order; it does not limit which adapters are registered. To exclude an adapter, use adapters: { <name>: false } in the configuration. Configuration explains adapter options and the strata: key prefix used by localStorage and sessionStorage since 3.0.
documents.s: ⚙️ Configure one instance for your app #

documents.t: The core API works without a provider. For a framework, create an instance with defineStorage() and bind it: React: bind hooks with createStrataHooks(). Vue: bind composables with createStrataComposables(). Angular: provide an instance through provideStrata(). On iOS and Android, register the Capacitor adapters, run yarn cap sync, and verify reads and writes on a device. A browser test does not exercise Keychain, EncryptedSharedPreferences, SQLite or the native filesystem. Follow the device verification guide.
documents.s: 📱 Choose a framework or native guide #

documents.t: Encryption and compression are opt-in and use the asynchronous API. Expiry supports absolute or sliding TTL. Queries filter stored values; Strata Storage remains client-side key-value storage, not a multi-user database. Key-prefix migration moves qualifying 2.x localStorage and sessionStorage keys on read, not in a bulk sweep. If one browser app only needs localStorage, use it directly.
Open the API reference for method and option contracts, or try the basic usage examples for another round-trip.
All notable changes to Strata Storage will be documented in this file. The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

The optional Firebase adapter names firestore and realtime are now accepted by the public TypeScript storage option after the integration registers them. Runtime behavior is unchanged. The package README's release summary and maintainer workflow match the current process.
Documentation only: no code, API or dist/ change.
README: the CI badge is gone (releases are built and verified locally; there is no hosted CI), and the Limitations section says the gates run before every release.
No JavaScript or API change: dist/ is equivalent to 3.1.1's.
The postinstall script. Installing the package no longer runs anything in your project; the setup steps it printed (including npx cap sync for Capacitor apps) are in the README's Quick Start.

The npx strata-storage CLI moved from scripts/ to bin/. The command is unchanged. Android: the fallback compileSdkVersion and targetSdkVersion (used only when your app does not set them) are now 36. Your app's own values still win. Build and gates: tsc + tsc-alias replace the custom build script, and yarn gates runs typecheck, lint, build and a Vitest suite against the built dist/ (the storage-ownership predicate and the README version row).

Same-key raw imports preserve the migrated value (ISSUE-14). When keyPrefix: false makes the named raw source and destination the same physical key, importRawSync now keeps the newly written Strata envelope instead of deleting it. Distinct-key imports still remove the source only after the destination write succeeds.

importRawSync(rawKey, key, options) — adopt ONE foreign localStorage / sessionStorage entry, named by its exact physical key, into a strata key, deleting the original. The migration path for data written by something other than this library (a pre-strata zustand store, a raw setItem), which the implicit paths deliberately never adopt. The raw string is kept as-is; an existing value at key wins and nothing is moved. Found while moving ZTools' 22 zustand stores onto strata.

sessionStorage keys were not prefixed (ISSUE-13). 3.0.0 documented both web areas as written under strata:, but SessionStorageAdapter's constructor defaulted its prefix to '', overriding the shared default. It now uses DEFAULT_WEB_KEY_PREFIX; existing bare envelope keys migrate themselves on read.

Android: consuming apps on current AGP failed to configure :strata-storage (ISSUE-12). android/build.gradle referenced getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android.txt'), which current Android Gradle Plugin versions reject at configuration time because it includes -dontoptimize — so the whole app build failed even though the library sets minifyEnabled false. Now uses proguard-android-optimize.txt, like every official Capacitor plugin. No JavaScript or API change.

:::danger Breaking — web adapter keys are now prefixed localStorage and sessionStorage keys are written under strata:. Existing data migrates itself on read, so most consumers do nothing — but set keyPrefix: false if anything outside this library reads a physical key directly (a pre-paint theme script, a logger reading its own level). Migration keeps the data reachable through this library; it cannot fix a hard-coded reader. :::

localStorage/sessionStorage default to the strata: key prefix (DEFAULT_WEB_KEY_PREFIX, exported). 2.9.0 made an unprefixed keyspace safe — a key is ours only if its value is a StorageValue envelope — and this makes it tidy too, so our keys are identifiable by name. cookies (already strata_), indexedDB, cache, memory and url are unchanged: none of them share a keyspace with other scripts. namespace is unaffected and composes as <keyPrefix><namespace>:<key>.

keyPrefix — false (or '') restores pre-3.0 behaviour; a string sets your own prefix. A per-adapter adapters.localStorage.prefix still wins. migrateLegacyKeys (default true) — adopt pre-3.0 unprefixed entries on read.

A miss at strata:<key> falls back to the bare <key>; if the value is one of ours it is moved under the prefix and returned. Three properties, each verified in a browser: Per key, on read — never a bulk sweep. A sweep would adopt every unprefixed envelope on the origin, including keys belonging to an instance that opted out or a sibling app still on 2.x. Never adopts a value that is not ours. A third-party key such as Microsoft Clarity's _cltk is left exactly where it is. Never overwrites. A value already at the prefixed key wins; the legacy entry is left alone. Two applications sharing one origin with one still on 2.x: set migrateLegacyKeys: false on the upgraded one, or better, give each a namespace — they were already colliding before this release.
A live timer no longer keeps a Node process alive. A short-lived script that created an instance and never called close() did not exit — measured hanging until killed at 120s, now exits immediately.
Closes the entire consumer-reported issue queue. No API changes and no data migration — every key stays exactly where it is.

Web adapters no longer treat other applications' keys as their own. localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies are shared with every script on the origin, and the default key prefix is empty — so a name test matched every key there. An adapter now identifies its own data by shape: a key is its own only when the stored value is a StorageValue envelope. This ends the Failed to get key … is not valid JSON error stream (Microsoft Clarity's _cltk was the usual trigger), keeps keys() to keys this library wrote, and closes two data-loss paths — the TTL sweep deleting a foreign key whose JSON carried an expired expires, and an unfiltered clear() wiping the origin. See Troubleshooting and Configuration ▸ key ownership. An unscoped subscribe() no longer throws. It fanned out across every registered adapter and indexedDB threw NotSupportedError, commonly killing application boot. Non-observable backends are skipped. See subscribe(). Per-adapter configuration reaches the adapter. defineStorage({ adapters: { localStorage: { prefix: 'app:' } } }) was a silent no-op on the synchronous path, which is usable before initialize() resolves. Configuration is now applied synchronously at registration. defaultStorages protects the synchronous path too — with localStorage unavailable, setSync now falls through to the next listed backend instead of throwing. clear({ expiredOnly: true }) was a guaranteed no-op on localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies, and cleanupExpired() reported 0 while doing the work. Both corrected. setLogLevel / getLogLevel are now exported. They were documented but unreachable — and they matter now, because skipped foreign keys are reported at debug. Documentation corrections. The localStorage adapter page said prefix defaults to 'strata_'; it defaults to ''. The Capacitor preferences page documented a prefix option that does not exist.

adapters: { <name>: false } now skips registration, not just initialization. Note that defaultStorages is not a registration list — it picks the default adapter, while multi-adapter operations span everything registered.
A real default key prefix for the web adapters, built on this release's shape check, with migrate-on-read and an opt-out for consumers whose physical key names are frozen.

README, packaging and metadata pass. The at-a-glance version row no longer ships stale, CHANGELOG.md is included in the tarball, funding and a canonical repository.url were added, and homepage points at this documentation site. dist/package.json was reduced to a two-field module marker so a publish from dist/ cannot ship the wrong tree. No runtime code changes across 2.8.2–2.8.5. :::caution 2.8.2 was a bad release 2.8.2 was published from a stale tree: its bundled docs omitted the required npx cap sync native setup step. It is deprecated on npm. Use 2.8.3 or later. :::

Documentation and metadata release — no runtime code changes, no API changes. Bug reports now route to GitHub Issues; the AI Integration Guide documents the npx cap sync native step, the registerCapacitorAdapters() helper, and the TypeScript moduleResolution: "bundler" | "nodenext" requirement for subpath types. See the root CHANGELOG.md for the full list.

License change: Apache-2.0 → MIT. A loosening of terms requiring no code changes on your part — the only condition is retaining the copyright and license notice. Versions at or before 2.7.1 remain available under Apache-2.0; 2.8.0 and later are MIT.

Audit-driven correctness and truthfulness release. No public API surface was removed beyond dead config; the focus is making documented behavior match the code. See the root CHANGELOG.md for the full itemized list.

Combined compress + encrypt pipeline now round-trips correctly. clear({ olderThan }), key/value validation, and close() state reset behave as documented. import()/snapshot() round-trip metadata; auto-backup no longer self-nests. QueryOptions (limit/skip/sort/select) are honored and query() decodes results; multi-adapter TTL cleanup and namespace key isolation work. Encryption works in Node/SSR environments.
Default storage order is now persistent-first. Compression is restricted to the lz algorithm — gzip was never implemented and the option type is now algorithm?: 'lz'.
Dead strategy config and the unused StorageStrategy type (type cleanup).

Documentation patch release: README and AI integration guide were refreshed to cover the 2.6.0 native parity features. Development dependency patch updates only; no runtime/API behavior changed from 2.6.0.

SQLite multi-store — the database and table options are now honored on iOS and Android, so multiple independent SQLite stores (distinct database files and/or tables) no longer collapse into a single physical table. Use separate defineStorage instances (or distinct database/table config) to keep stores isolated. Native filesystem backend — FilesystemAdapter now works on iOS and Android (it was previously unavailable on every platform). One file per key under the app's documents/files directory (strata_storage/), storing the full value wrapper as JSON, with atomic writes; isAvailable() now returns true. size(true) — native SQLite and filesystem backends now return the { keys, values, metadata } byte breakdown (the flag was previously ignored, returning only { total, count }).

SQLite value round-trip — native get now returns the full StorageValue wrapper ({ value, created, updated, expires, tags, metadata }) instead of a raw blob, so TTL, tags, and metadata survive a write→read cycle on iOS and Android. Corrupt/legacy rows are treated as a miss instead of throwing. Filesystem key/temp-file collision — in-flight temp files now live in a reserved staging subdirectory, so a key whose name resembles a temp file (e.g. "backup.tmp") is never skipped by keys()/size() or wrongly deleted by clear(). size().total consistency — native backends now include key bytes in total, matching the web adapters' convention. iOS SQLite bind safety — text/blob binds use SQLITE_TRANSIENT, removing a latent use-after-free for transient Swift buffers.

androidx.security:security-crypto upgraded 1.1.0-alpha06 → 1.1.0 (stable). The EncryptedSharedPreferences / MasterKey API is unchanged. The native SQLite database file now resolves from the database option (default strata_storage → strata_storage.db); table identifiers are sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9_]. Stored values remain bound parameters. Marketing website tooling migrated to Yarn 4 (Corepack).

The native iOS/Android changes in this release are code-complete and reviewed but require on-device verification — follow docs/guides/platforms/device-verification.md. Web/browser functionality is validated by the quality gates (typecheck + build + lint); the project ships no automated test runner.

Framework-agnostic, provider-free usage — defineStorage() returns a ready-to-use instance you can create once and use anywhere, with no Provider/DI required (Zustand-style). createStrataHooks(instance) (React), createStrataComposables(instance) (Vue), and provideStrata(instance) (Angular) bind to a created instance; the Provider/Plugin/Service APIs remain optional. Synchronous API — getSync/setSync/removeSync/hasSync/keysSync/ clearSync for sync-capable adapters (memory, localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, url). Async-only backends (indexedDB, cache, native) throw a clear error; sync set with encrypt/compress also throws (those are async). URL-state adapter (URLAdapter) — persist state in the query string (default) or hash fragment, with popstate/hashchange change events. Disaster recovery (all opt-in) — FNV-1a integrity checksums with corruption detection, durable write-verify-readback, mirroring to backup adapters with read-repair, and snapshot()/restore() plus scheduled autoBackup. Exported integrity helpers (computeChecksum/verifyChecksum) and error classes (e.g. IntegrityError) for instanceof use.

The React/Vue/Angular entry points are now actually built and shipped — strata-storage/react|vue|angular previously resolved to files that were never compiled into dist/, so every framework import failed. Multi-adapter operations (keys/clear/size/subscribe with no explicit storage) now span all registered adapters instead of only the default. Cross-tab sync now applies received changes to local memory/IndexedDB/cache adapters (previously broadcasts were sent but never applied). AES-CBC now uses a correct 16-byte IV. Security: prototype-pollution guards in deep-merge/import/restore, ReDoS-capped regex, and SameSite=Lax + automatic Secure cookie defaults. iOS native plugin now registers with Capacitor (it had no registration and was non-functional); added missing native methods on iOS and Android; Keychain accessibility hardened.

All diagnostic output now routes through a level-gated internal logger (default warn); the library no longer writes to the consumer console by default. Toggle with new Strata({ debug: { enabled: true } }). Dependencies updated to latest stable (including TypeScript 6 and ESLint 10). The default instance initializes lazily, so importing the package performs no I/O. Current quality gates are typecheck, build, lint, and CI; the project no longer ships an automated test runner.

One key/value API over browser and Capacitor adapters. The chosen adapter determines persistence and platform availability. The core package has no runtime dependencies; React, Vue, Angular, Firebase and Capacitor integrations have optional peers.

The standard browser instance registers memory, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies and a Cache-backed JSON-value adapter. Capacitor iOS and Android apps can register Preferences, Secure, SQLite and Filesystem adapters. React Native is not a supported native adapter runtime. Node or SSR code cannot assume browser or Capacitor globals exist.

defineStorage() and the exported storage singleton register standard web adapters and initialize on first use. A manual new Strata() instance needs adapter registration before initialization or operations. import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); await storage.set('draft', 'First pass');

Use JSON-serializable strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, plain objects and null. undefined, functions, symbols and circular references are not supported values. A Date becomes a JSON string; reconstruct a Date in your application if you need one.

There is no single package-wide quota. Browser policy, browsing mode, data size and available device space affect limits; native storage has its own constraints. maxSize can be configured for the memory adapter, but it does not reserve that amount of RAM. Handle write failures and test representative values on each platform.

No. To encrypt a value, configure encryption on the instance and supply an encryption password in the write flow. A per-write encrypt: true flag on an instance without enabled encryption does not create an encryptor. Never bundle a fixed password in browser JavaScript. Native Secure storage uses iOS Keychain or Android EncryptedSharedPreferences after Capacitor registration; Strata does not expose a biometric requirement. See the encryption guide.

No. Browser, iOS and Android adapters store values locally. Browser cross-tab sync can notify another tab about supported changes but does not create a cross-device account or settle concurrent writes. Firebase is an optional integration with separate setup and authentication.

documents.t: query() tests fields of each decoded value. It does not treat the storage key or Strata wrapper metadata as fields. If a value contains { tags: ['work'], score: 80 }, a supported condition is: const matches = await storage.query({ tags: { $in: ['work'] }, score: { $gte: 80 }, }); Use keys('prefix') or keys(/^prefix/) when the key name is what you need to filter.

Common issues and solutions when using Strata Storage.
Installation Issues Runtime Errors Platform-Specific Issues Performance Issues Data Persistence Issues TypeScript Issues

Problem: npm install strata-storage fails with package not found error. Solution: # Clear npm cache npm cache clean --force # Try installing again npm install strata-storage # Or use specific version npm install strata-storage@latest

Problem: Warnings about missing peer dependencies. Solution: Peer dependencies are optional. Install only what you need: # For React projects npm install react # For Vue projects npm install vue # For Angular projects npm install @angular/core # For Capacitor projects npm install @capacitor/core

Problem: Native module build errors on iOS/Android. Solution: # iOS: Update CocoaPods cd ios && pod update && cd .. # Android: Clean gradle cache cd android && ./gradlew clean && cd .. # Sync Capacitor npx cap sync

Problem: A manually constructed Strata instance has no registered adapters, or the requested adapter is unavailable. Solution: Use defineStorage() for the standard web adapters. It initializes lazily: import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage'; const storage = defineStorage(); await storage.set('key', 'value');

Symptom. On every page load, one or more of: [strata-storage] Failed to get key _cltk from sessionStorage: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 's', "ts3hsf" is not valid JSON [strata-storage] Failed to get key logger-level from localStorage: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'w', "warn" is not valid JSON Fixed in 2.9.0 — upgrade. yarn up strata-storage (or npm i strata-storage@latest). No code change and no migration: your keys stay exactly where they are. What was happening. localStorage and sessionStorage are shared with every other script on the origin, and the web adapters' key prefix was empty before 3.0.0 — so the adapter's name test matched every key on the origin, including third-party ones. It then parsed each as JSON and reported the failure at error level. _cltk is Microsoft Clarity's session key; the trigger is usually an analytics tag, not your code. Consumers routing their logger into Sentry received one report per foreign key per sweep. Two further consequences, both closed by the same fix: keys() returned keys the library never wrote, and the TTL sweep could delete a foreign key whose JSON happened to carry an expired expires. After 2.9.0 an adapter treats a key as its own only when the stored value is a StorageValue envelope. Foreign keys are skipped silently — a value that is not ours is evidence the key belongs to somebody else, not an error. To see what is being skipped: import { setLogLevel } from 'strata-storage'; setLogLevel('debug'); // [strata-storage] sessionStorage: skipping key "_cltk" — value is not readable as // sessionStorage data (not written by this adapter). If you cannot upgrade yet, raise the log level's floor so error output is suppressed (setLogLevel('silent') — note this silences real errors too), or construct Strata directly and register only the adapters you use. Neither is needed on 2.9.0.

documents.t: Symptom. storage.subscribe(cb) with no options throws, often taking application boot with it: NotSupportedError: Operation 'subscribe' is not supported by indexedDB adapter Fixed in 2.9.0 — upgrade. The unscoped form fanned out across every registered adapter, and indexedDB, cookies and cache cannot emit change events — so the documented "hear every adapter" form failed on any default instance. Non-observable backends are now skipped, and you get an observer attached to the ones that can speak. Workaround before 2.9.0 (still valid, and tighter when you only care about one backend): storage.subscribe(cb, { storage: 'localStorage' });

documents.t: Problem: Browser storage quota exceeded. Solution: import { QuotaExceededError } from 'strata-storage'; try { await storage.set('data', largeData); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof QuotaExceededError) { // Option 1: Clear old data await storage.clear(); // Option 2: Use compression await storage.set('data', largeData, { compress: true }); // Option 3: Switch to IndexedDB await storage.set('data', largeData, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); } }

Problem: Encryption/decryption fails. Solution: // Ensure encryption is properly configured const storage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true, password: 'your-password' // Use consistent password } }); // Don't change password after storing encrypted data // or you won't be able to decrypt it

Problem: Requested storage adapter not available. Solution: // Check available storage types first const storage = defineStorage(); const available = storage.getAvailableStorageTypes(); console.log('Available:', available); // Use available storage type if (available.includes('indexedDB')) { await storage.set('key', 'value', { storage: 'indexedDB' }); } else { // Fallback to default await storage.set('key', 'value'); }

Private/Incognito Mode​ Problem: Storage not working in private browsing mode. Solution: Use memory adapter as fallback: const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorage: 'memory' // Works in all modes }); Safari localStorage Disabled​ Problem: localStorage disabled in Safari privacy settings. Solution: Automatic fallback is built-in, or configure manually: const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'memory'] // Skip localStorage }); Cross-Origin Issues​ Problem: Cannot access storage from different origin. Solution: Storage is origin-specific by design. Use postMessage for cross-origin: // In iframe window.parent.postMessage({ key: 'value' }, '*'); // In parent window.addEventListener('message', (event) => { await storage.set(event.data.key, event.data.value); });

Keychain Access Denied​ Problem: Cannot access Keychain storage on iOS. Solution: Add usage description to Info.plist: <key>NSFaceIDUsageDescription</key> <string>This app uses secure storage to protect your data</string> Data Lost After App Update​ Problem: Data disappears after updating app. Solution: Don't use .tmp or .cache directories: // Use UserDefaults or Keychain for persistent data await storage.set('key', 'value', { storage: 'preferences' }); SQLite Permission Denied​ Problem: Cannot create/access SQLite database. Solution: Ensure using correct directory: // Use documents directory, not tmp await storage.set('key', 'value', { storage: 'sqlite' });

SharedPreferences Encryption Fails​ Problem: EncryptedSharedPreferences throws error. Solution: Requires Android 6.0+ (API 23): import { Capacitor } from '@capacitor/core'; if (Capacitor.getPlatform() === 'android') { // Check Android version const version = await Capacitor.getAndroidVersion(); if (version >= 23) { await storage.set('key', 'value', { storage: 'secure' }); } else { // Fallback for older Android await storage.set('key', 'value', { encrypt: true }); } } SQLite Database Locked​ Problem: Database is locked error. Solution: Ensure proper connection management: // Don't open multiple connections const storage = defineStorage(); // Reuse instance // Use throughout app await storage.set('key', 'value');

Problem: Writing data is slow. Solution: // Start independent writes together await Promise.all([ storage.set('key1', 'value1'), storage.set('key2', 'value2'), storage.set('key3', 'value3') ]); // Disable compression for small data await storage.set('small', 'value', { compress: false }); // Use faster storage adapter await storage.set('key', 'value', { storage: 'memory' });

Problem: Reading data is slow. Solution: // Use memory caching const storage = defineStorage({ cache: { enabled: true, maxSize: 100 // Cache 100 items } }); // Read multiple keys at once const values = await Promise.all( ['key1', 'key2', 'key3'].map((key) => storage.get(key)) );

Problem: App uses too much memory. Solution: // Limit cache size const storage = defineStorage({ cache: { enabled: true, maxSize: 50 // Smaller cache } }); // Don't store large objects in memory adapter // Use IndexedDB or SQLite instead await storage.set('large', bigData, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); // Clear memory periodically await storage.clear({ storage: 'memory' });

Problem: Data disappears after page reload. Solution: // Don't use sessionStorage or memory for persistent data await storage.set('key', 'value', { storage: 'localStorage' // Persists across sessions }); // Or use default (picks best persistent storage) await storage.set('key', 'value');

Problem: Browser update clears storage. Solution: Use multiple storage locations: // Store in both localStorage and IndexedDB await storage.set('important', value, { storage: 'localStorage' }); await storage.set('important', value, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); // Implement backup async function backupData() { const keys = await storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'indexedDB' }); const data = Object.fromEntries(await Promise.all( keys.map(async (key) => [key, await storage.get(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' })]) )); return data; // Encrypt and transfer through your own authenticated backup API. }

Problem: Data not automatically removed after TTL. Solution: Ensure TTL cleanup is enabled: const storage = defineStorage({ ttl: { autoCleanup: true, cleanupInterval: 60000 // Check every minute } }); // Verify TTL is set correctly await storage.set('temp', 'value', { ttl: 5000 // 5 seconds }); // Wait and check setTimeout(async () => { const value = await storage.get('temp'); // Should be null console.log(value); }, 6000);

Problem: TypeScript type errors. Solution: // Use generic types interface User { id: number; name: string; } const storage = defineStorage(); // Type-safe operations await storage.set<User>('user', { id: 1, name: 'John' }); const user = await storage.get<User>('user'); // user is typed as User | null if (user) { console.log(user.name); // Type-safe }

Problem: Import errors or missing types. Solution: // Ensure types are imported correctly import { defineStorage, type StrataConfig } from 'strata-storage'; // Or use namespace imports import * as StrataStorage from 'strata-storage'; const storage = StrataStorage.defineStorage();

Problem: Type errors in React/Vue/Angular. Solution: // React import { useStrata } from 'strata-storage/react'; function MyComponent() { const { data, loading, error } = useStrata<string>('key'); // data is typed as string | null } // Vue import { useStrata } from 'strata-storage/vue'; interface MyData { value: string; } const { data, loading } = useStrata<MyData>('key'); // data is Ref<MyData | null>
